front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) in California. It turns the licensing requirements of Title 22 of the California Code of Regulations (22 CCR), the RCFE Act in the Health and Safety Code (HSC), and related statutes into written policies and step-by-step procedures that staff can follow every day.

The manual is meant to:

- Protect the dignity, personal rights, health and safety of every resident.
- Give administrators, staff and volunteers one consistent reference for admission, care, medication assistance, staffing, training, reporting, emergency response and business operations.
- Support the Plan of Operation and the Section B supporting documents that CDSS Community Care Licensing (CCL) reviews with a license application (LIC 281).
- Show licensing staff, the governing body and other reviewers that each regulatory requirement has a written policy and a responsible person.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

This manual is a template. Before use, it **must be customized** for [AGENCY NAME]:

- Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and other bracketed field with facility-specific information. This includes the facility name, address, licensed capacity, administrator and designated substitute, staffing pattern, evacuation and relocation sites, and local contacts.
- Confirm that each policy reflects what the facility actually does. Delete or adapt any policy that does not apply, for example one for a service the facility does not offer.

The customized manual **must be formally adopted by the governing body** of [AGENCY NAME]. Record the adoption date, the approving authority and the version in the manual's adoption record.

The manual **must be kept current**. Review it at least annually. Also review it whenever a regulation, statute or CDSS form changes, after an incident or inspection finding that shows a gap, and whenever the facility changes its operations, capacity or services. Date every revision and retire superseded copies.

**Staff must be trained on the manual.** Every employee, and every volunteer who works with residents, must be trained on the policies that apply to their duties before they work independently. They must also be retrained when policies change. Training must be documented in personnel records. This manual supplements the regulatory training requirements and does not replace them.

This manual is an operational tool and not legal advice. When a policy and a regulation appear to conflict, the current regulation controls. Seek legal or employment counsel where the manual says to.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### Who should use it

- **Administrator and designated substitute:** the primary owners of the manual, responsible for customization, annual review, and making sure policies are followed.
- **Direct care staff:** use the policies on resident rights, admission and appraisal, medication assistance, incident and abuse reporting, night supervision, dementia care, infection control and emergency response.
- **Governing body or owner:** adopts the manual, approves revisions, and uses it to oversee compliance.
- **Licensing reviewers:** can use Appendix A to find the policy that satisfies each item on the official checklist.

### How the manual is organized

Each policy states its purpose, the regulatory basis (by exact cite), who is responsible, and the procedure to follow. Required forms, posted notices, timelines and documentation are called out inside the relevant policy. Policies are arranged to follow the order of the Section B items in LIC 281, so the manual can be assembled as an application packet: B1, B2, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 (only if the water supply is private), B13, B14, B15, B16, B17. Operational policies that LIC 281 does not list follow the Section B policies.

### Steps for putting the manual into service

1. **Customize.** Replace every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder and bracketed field. Add the facility's real names, phone numbers, sites, schedules and rates.
2. **Check consistency.** Reviewers compare documents against each other. Job descriptions (B4) must match the LIC 500. Work hours in the personnel policies (B5) must match the personnel reports. Exit routes on the LIC 999 must match the LIC 610 emergency plan.
3. **Verify against current rules and forms.** Confirm each cited rule and the current edition of each CDSS form.
4. **Adopt.** Obtain governing-body approval and record the date.
5. **Train.** Train all staff, document the training and keep sign-off records in personnel files.
6. **Make it available.** Keep a complete copy where staff can read it at any time. Post or keep readily available the items the regulations require, such as emergency exit plans, emergency telephone numbers and the admission agreement or a notice of its availability.
7. **Maintain.** Review at least annually and after any regulatory change, incident or inspection finding. Log each revision with its date.

### Using Appendix A

Appendix A is the crosswalk to the official LIC 281 checklist. Each official item (A1-A16 and B1-B17, with sub-items numbered in bullet order, e.g. B7.1) is listed next to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to prepare a license application packet, to answer a reviewer's question, and to find gaps. If an item has no matching policy, add one before submitting.

### Conventions

- **Bracketed text** such as [AGENCY NAME] must be replaced before adoption.
- **Cites** (e.g., 22 CCR §87211) are given in exact form so staff can look up the full rule.
- **"Applies only if"** notes mark policies that are conditional, such as the Assisted Living Waiver, dementia advertising, hospice waiver, private water supply and resident cash handling.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

[AGENCY NAME] operates as a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) licensed by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Community Care Licensing Division. The rules below are the ones this manual is built on. They are cited exactly as given and summarized briefly. Staff should consult the full text of each rule through the linked source.

### Governing rules

**Title 22, California Code of Regulations (RCFE regulations)**

- **22 CCR §87468.1** (Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities): 18 personal rights, including dignity, freedom from abuse, how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman, and the right to leave and to refuse care. Subsection (b) bars discrimination based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive those protections.
- **22 CCR §87212** (Emergency Disaster Plan): a written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan, with exit plans and telephone numbers posted.
- **22 CCR §87411** (Personnel Requirements-General): sufficient and competent staff, training, first aid, health screening and criminal record clearance.
- **22 CCR §87465** (Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services): medication assistance limits, PRN orders, storage, destruction and records, first aid kit and emergency numbers.
- **22 CCR §87507** (Admission Agreements): content, format and timing of the written admission agreement.
- **22 CCR §87615** (Prohibited Health Conditions): conditions that bar admission or retention.
- **22 CCR §87211** (Reporting Requirements): incident, outbreak, fire, abuse, financial-distress and administrator-change reports, with their timeframes.
- **22 CCR §87415** (Night Supervision (RCFE)): night staffing by facility size.
- **22 CCR §87705** (Care of Persons with Dementia): awake night supervision for residents with dementia in homes with fewer than 16 beds.
- **22 CCR §87706** (Advertising Dementia Special Care): written dementia program and advertisement retention. Applies if the facility advertises dementia care.
- **22 CCR §87208** (Plan of Operation): required content of the written plan of operation.
- **22 CCR §87202** (Fire Clearance): fire clearance before licensure and before accepting nonambulatory or bedridden residents.
- **22 CCR §87307** (Personal Accommodations and Services): bedroom occupancy and toilet, washbasin and bathing fixture ratios.
- **22 CCR §87303** (Maintenance and Operation): heat, hot water, plant maintenance and private water supply testing.
- **22 CCR §87355** (Criminal Record Clearance): DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption.
- **22 CCR §87217** (Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables): records, a separate account, and LIC 400 and LIC 402 if the facility holds resident cash.
- **22 CCR §87405** (Administrator-Qualifications and Duties): qualifications, certification, on-premises hours and a designated substitute.
- **22 CCR §87470** (Infection Control Requirements): written infection control plan (LIC 9282), Infection Control Lead, training and review.
- **22 CCR §87632** (Hospice Care Waiver): written request and CDSS decision timeline.
- **22 CCR §87457** (Pre-Admission Appraisal): pre-admission interview, evaluation and suitability determination.

**Health and Safety Code (RCFE Act)**

- **HSC §1569.616** (Administrator certification): initial certification program and exam, and continuing education.
- **HSC §1569.625** (Direct care staff training): initial and annual training hours and required topics.
- **HSC §1569.626** (Dementia training for direct care staff): initial and annual dementia training hours.
- **HSC §1569.69** (Medication assistance training): initial and annual training and exam, by facility size.
- **HSC §1569.605** (Liability insurance minimums): $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate.
- **HSC §1569.185** (License fees): annual license fee, late fee and capacity change fee.

**Other statutes, regulations and application instructions**

- **W&I Code §15630** (Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting): staff are mandated reporters. The facility-specific timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c).
- **42 CFR §441.301(c)** (HCBS Settings Rule): applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver.
- **Labor Code §246** (Paid sick leave): at least 40 hours or 5 days per year.
- **IWC Wage Order 5** (Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly): special rules for a sole caregiver. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel.
- **LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B** (application attachments): includes the theft and loss policy (B14), neighborhood complaint policy (B15), sample menu (B10) and job descriptions and personnel policies (B4-B5).

### Regulators and contacts

| **CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau** | RCFE administrator certificates, exams, CE vendors | 916-653-9300; AdminCertInfo@dss.ca.gov; https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/community-care/administrator-certification/administrator-information |
| **California Department of Aging, Long-Term Care Ombudsman** | Resident advocacy; receives mandated abuse reports from long-term care facilities | 1-800-231-4024 (CRISISline); https://www.aging.ca.gov/Programs/LTCOP/ |
| **Local fire authority / State Fire Marshal** | Fire clearance before licensure and before accepting nonambulatory or bedridden residents | No central phone or email is listed. Contact the fire authority for the facility's jurisdiction. See 22 CCR §87202: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/22-CCR-87202 |
| **DHCS, Assisted Living Waiver (Integrated Systems of Care Division)** | Medi-Cal ALW provider enrollment, tier rates, waiver oversight. Relevant only if the facility enrolls in the ALW. | ProFacWAIVER@dhcs.ca.gov; WaiveProEnroll@dhcs.ca.gov; https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/long-term-care-alternatives-home-and-community-based-service-options/assisted-living-waiver/ (no phone listed) |

Reports to the licensing agency, the local ombudsman, local law enforcement, the local health officer and the person responsible for the resident must follow the methods and timeframes in 22 CCR §87211 and W&I Code §15630. Record the local ombudsman, health officer, law enforcement and fire contacts for [AGENCY NAME]'s county in the facility's emergency contact list.

### Official policy checklist and application document

CDSS reviews this manual and the license application against **LIC 281, Application Instructions for a Facility License**, issued by CDSS Community Care Licensing Division. The reviewer uses LIC 281 as the packet checklist:

- **Section A** lists the LIC forms (items A1-A16).
- **Section B** lists the plan-of-operation documents and policies (items B1-B17).

**Appendix A maps every official LIC 281 item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it.** Use it to confirm that each Section A and Section B item is covered. Sub-items inside a B item are numbered in bullet order (for example, B7.1). Items that apply only to other facility types (A9.A, A17, B3, B18) are omitted.

Points to keep in mind when using LIC 281:

- LIC 281 has no single plan-of-operation form. The application fee plus the Section A and Section B documents go to the licensing agency as one packet, in the same sequence as the booklet. An incomplete packet is returned in full. All forms need original signatures and dates, and the applicant should keep a photocopy.
- The reviewer compares documents against each other. Job descriptions (B4) must match the LIC 500. Work hours in the personnel policies (B5) must match the personnel reports. Exit routes on the LIC 999 must match the LIC 610 plan.
- B15 (neighborhood complaint policy) is marked Required for RCFE in the table, but its text limits it to facilities of six or fewer that are not owner-occupied.
- B7 says its double-asterisk items may also appear in "Section B10 - Admission Policies". This most likely means B9, so check the item against the current booklet. B9 includes a group-home intake bullet and B8's discipline detail applies to group homes and FFAs only. Neither applies to an RCFE.
- **Edition caution:** the CDSS forms page lists LIC 281 (11/25) as current. The item numbering used here comes from the LIC 281 (9/04) text, which matches the owner-supplied text, because the 11/25 PDF could not be retrieved. **Compare the numbering against the current edition before filing.** Current edition: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Portals/9/Additional-Resources/Forms-and-Brochures/2020/I-L/LIC281.pdf
- Newer program-specific content, such as the infection control plan (22 CCR §87470) and the dementia and hospice waivers (22 CCR §87706, 22 CCR §87632), is not in LIC 281. This manual supplements the LIC 281 items with the Title 22 sections above, including 22 CCR §87208 (plan of operation).

### Keeping the framework current

This manual must be customized for [AGENCY NAME] (all [AGENCY NAME] placeholders replaced), adopted by the governing body, kept current as rules and forms change, and taught to all staff, with training documented. Verify each cite and each form edition against the official source before relying on this summary. Where employment or legal questions arise, such as live-in shifts under IWC Wage Order 5, consult qualified counsel.

citations.title: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities
citations.requirement: Lists 18 personal rights: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation or abuse; being told how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman; leaving at any time and not being locked in; private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care; moving out. Subsection (b) bars denial of admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, and association, based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive the (b) protections.

citations.title: Emergency Disaster Plan
citations.requirement: A written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan. It must cover: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notifying a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements-General
citations.requirement: Personnel must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need. Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. Staff assisting with personal ADLs get initial and annual training under HSC §§1569.625 and 1569.69, plus first aid from a qualified provider. Required training topics are listed, with trainer qualifications and documentation in personnel records. All personnel need a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan.

citations.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services
citations.requirement: Requires a plan for incidental medical and dental care. Staff may only assist with self-administered medications and may not give injections unless authorized by law. Assistance cannot include forcing, hiding or camouflaging medications. PRN rules: a signed, dated physician order on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours. Central storage in a locked place, in the original container, with a record kept at least 1 year. Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, with a record kept at least 3 years. First aid kit; emergency numbers posted; ambulance number available; call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health.

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Individual written agreement in 12-point type, plain language, with titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Copy given immediately, and a copy or notice of availability posted. Must specify basic services, additional services, rates, payment, 60 days' written notice of rate changes, refund conditions, preadmission fee limits and refunds, visiting policy, firearms policy, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman. LIC 9158 is required when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

citations.title: Prohibited Health Conditions
citations.requirement: Residents who need health services for, or have, these conditions cannot be admitted or retained: stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, and tracheostomies. The list is not exhaustive ("including, but not limited to").

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: (a)(1) Written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse). (a)(2) Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer. (a)(3) Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority, and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency. (b),(c) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours. (d),(e),(f) Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice; notice to applicants before signing; civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. (g) Notice of a new administrator within 30 days. (h) Change of chief corporate officer within 15 working days.

citations.title: Night Supervision (RCFE)
citations.requirement: Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight. 16–100 residents: one employee awake on duty plus one on call within 10 minutes. Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained. (Per fact-checked research S7.)

citations.title: Care of Persons with Dementia
citations.requirement: In homes with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation. (Per fact-checked research S8.)

citations.title: Advertising Dementia Special Care
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises dementia care must have a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep advertisements for 3 years. (Per fact-checked research S27 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan. (Per fact-checked research S23.)

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Fire clearance is required before licensure. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. (Per fact-checked research S28.)

citations.title: Personal Accommodations and Services
citations.requirement: No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family. (Per fact-checked research S24.)

citations.title: Maintenance and Operation
citations.requirement: Heat of at least 68°F; hot water 105–120°F; plant maintenance standards; private water supply testing (annually for capacity 7–15). (Per fact-checked research S69 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and staff before they work or are present. (Per fact-checked research S29.)

citations.title: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables
citations.requirement: If the facility holds resident cash, it must keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as the residents' money, with no commingling. LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond. (Per fact-checked research S70.)

citations.title: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character, and must be certified. Added education and experience for 16+ beds. Must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent. (Per fact-checked research S14.)

citations.title: Infection Control Requirements
citations.requirement: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282). Name an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional. Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request. (Per fact-checked research S32.)

citations.title: Hospice Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request. (Per fact-checked research S26.)

citations.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal
citations.requirement: Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination against admission criteria before admission. (Per fact-checked research S35 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Administrator certification
citations.requirement: 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days. 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. (Per fact-checked research S13.)

citations.title: Direct care staff training
citations.requirement: 40 hours initial: 20 before working alone and 20 within 4 weeks. The first 20 include 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. 20 hours annually, including 8 hours dementia. (Per fact-checked research S10.)

citations.title: Dementia training for direct care staff
citations.requirement: Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S11.)

citations.title: Medication assistance training
citations.requirement: Homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+: 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S12.)

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: Care custodians and facility staff are mandated reporters. Report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then in writing within the statutory time (SOC 341). The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c). (Per fact-checked research S36.)

citations.title: Liability insurance minimums
citations.requirement: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence. (Per fact-checked research S18.)

citations.title: HCBS Settings Rule (applies to Assisted Living Waiver settings)
citations.requirement: HCBS settings must include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors. Applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver. (Per fact-checked research.)

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Annual fee of $495.60 (4–6 beds) or $742.80 (7–15 beds), due each license anniversary, with a 50% late fee. Capacity change fee of $25. (Per fact-checked research S1.)

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: At least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year. (Per fact-checked research S57.)

citations.title: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly
citations.requirement: Special meal and rest period rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel. (Per fact-checked research S60.)

citations.cite: LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B
citations.title: Application attachments (theft and loss policy B14; neighborhood complaint policy B15; sample menu B10; job descriptions B4–B5)
citations.requirement: Written theft and loss policy (B14); neighborhood complaint policy when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer (B15); sample menu (B10); job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5). (Per fact-checked research S21.)

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: License Application and Applicant Forms (LIC 200, 215, 308, 309)
policies.applies_to: Licensee/applicants, governing body, designated administrator, and anyone preparing or reviewing the license application packet
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits a complete, correctly signed set of applicant identification and responsibility forms to the CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, so the Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) application is not returned or delayed for form errors.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will complete and submit the following forms with its RCFE license application, exactly as required by the CDSS Application Instructions for a Facility License (LIC 281), Section A. This policy meets LIC 281 item A1 (LIC 200, Application for a Community Care Facility or Residential Care Facility for the Elderly License): the form is filled out completely, every applicant signs including each general partner, signatures are originals (no photocopied signatures), signatures match the applicant's name unless the applicant is a corporation or LLC, and a corporation attaches the Board resolution authorizing the signers. This policy meets LIC 281 item A2 (LIC 215, Applicant Information): one form per applicant, original signatures, and current reference statements that are not from relatives. This policy meets LIC 281 item A3 (LIC 308, Designation of Facility (Administrative) Responsibility): at least one individual is designated to act in the licensee's absence, the licensee does not designate himself or herself, an entity applicant attaches a resolution authorizing the delegation, and signatures are originals. This policy meets LIC 281 item A4 (LIC 309, Administrative Organization): the form is submitted only if the applicant is a corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC, its information matches the LIC 200, and terms of office match the articles and bylaws. The non-refundable application fee is $990 for a 4-6 bed facility or $1,486.80 for a 7-15 bed facility, payable to CDSS. After licensure, the annual license fee ($495.60 for 4-6 beds; $742.80 for 7-15 beds) is due on each license anniversary; a 50% late fee applies if it is paid late, and a $25 fee applies to a capacity change. Any person designated to act for the licensee on LIC 308, and any administrator, must meet the administrator qualifications and duties in 22 CCR §87405.

definitions.definition: Each individual, or the corporation, partnership, LLC or public agency, applying for the RCFE license. Each general partner is an applicant.
A handwritten signature in ink on the form itself. Photocopied or stamped signatures are not accepted.
A person named on LIC 308 to act for the licensee when the licensee is absent. The licensee may not name himself or herself.
The CDSS Adult and Senior Care Program unit that receives and processes new RCFE license applications.

procedures: The licensee/governing body identifies every applicant. For a partnership this means each general partner; for a corporation or LLC it means the entity and its authorized signer. The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] records the list in the application checklist.
Download the current LIC 200, LIC 215, LIC 308 and LIC 309 from the CDSS forms page and the LIC 281 instructions. Do not use outdated versions.

LIC 200 (A1): Complete every field. Each applicant, including each general partner, signs in ink. Check that each signature matches the applicant's printed name (unless the applicant is a corporation or LLC).
If the applicant is a corporation or LLC, obtain a signed Board resolution (or written delegation) authorizing the named signer to apply for the license and attach it to the LIC 200 (see SB-01).
LIC 215 (A2): Give one form to each applicant. Each applicant completes and signs it in ink.
Collect current reference statements for each LIC 215. Confirm that no reference is a relative of the applicant. Replace any statement that is dated too long ago to be current.
LIC 308 (A3): Select at least one qualified individual to act in the licensee's absence. Confirm that person is not the licensee and that he or she accepts the role.
Confirm the designee's qualifications, including the age and administrator requirements in 22 CCR §87405, and that the designee will complete the personnel forms in SA-04.
If the applicant is a corporation or LLC, attach the resolution authorizing the delegation to the LIC 308. The authorized signer signs the form in ink.
LIC 309 (A4): Determine whether it is required. Individual applicants do not submit it. A corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC does.
When LIC 309 is required, copy names, titles and offices from the LIC 200 and the entity documents. Confirm terms of office match the articles and bylaws.
Compare the LIC 200, LIC 215, LIC 308 and LIC 309 for consistent names, addresses, entity type and capacity. Resolve any mismatch before signing.
Prepare the application fee payment ($990 for 4-6 beds or $1,486.80 for 7-15 beds) to CDSS. Record the payment amount and check or reference number.
A second person who did not prepare the forms reviews them against this policy and the LIC 281 instructions, then initials the checklist (see FC-01).

Make a complete copy of the signed packet for the facility file. Mail the original packet to the Centralized Applications Bureau, 744 P Street, MS 9-14-8201, Sacramento, CA 95814, using a trackable method.
After licensure, the [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] calendars the license anniversary and pays the annual fee on time, and reports any capacity change with the $25 fee.

responsibilities.duty: Signs all forms in ink, adopts any required resolutions, designates the person to act in the licensee's absence, and pays the application and annual fees.
Prepares the forms, keeps the application checklist, and ensures the designee meets qualifications.
Accepts the designation on LIC 308 and acts for the licensee when the licensee is absent.
Checks the packet against LIC 281 before mailing and initials the checklist.

documentation: Signed originals of LIC 200, 215, 308 and 309 (as required), with copies in the facility license file
Board resolutions or written delegations authorizing signers and the designee
Reference statements attached to each LIC 215
Fee payment record and mailing tracking record
Completed application checklist with reviewer initials and date

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Resident Cash Resources Affidavit and Surety Bond (LIC 400, LIC 402)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, bookkeeping staff, and anyone who may handle resident money
policies.purpose: To state whether [AGENCY NAME] will hold resident cash, to complete the LIC 400 affidavit accurately, to obtain the LIC 402 surety bond when required, and to protect any resident money held under 22 CCR §87217.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will complete the LIC 400 and, if the facility will hold resident cash, will obtain and submit a LIC 402 surety bond. This policy meets LIC 281 item A5 (LIC 400, Affidavit Regarding Client Cash Resources): the form is completed with the appropriate box checked, a bond is obtained if the box indicates the facility will hold resident cash, and the form carries original signatures. This policy meets LIC 281 item A6 (LIC 402, Surety Bond): the bond uses the LIC 402 language, identifies the State of California as beneficiary, shows effective and expiration dates, carries original seals and signatures, and is in an amount that matches the amount on the LIC 400. If [AGENCY NAME] holds resident cash, it will keep receipts and accounting records and will hold the money in a separate account titled as the residents' money, never commingled with facility operating funds, as required by 22 CCR §87217. Resident funds handling after licensure is also governed by RR-04.

definitions.definition: Money belonging to residents that the facility holds or manages on their behalf.
A bond naming the State of California as beneficiary that protects resident funds held by the facility.
Mixing resident money with facility operating money or any other funds. It is not permitted.

procedures: Before applying, the licensee and administrator decide in writing whether the facility will hold any resident cash, and record the decision in the governing body minutes.
Obtain the current LIC 400 and LIC 402 forms from CDSS.
Complete the LIC 400 and check the box that accurately reflects the decision. The licensee signs in ink; no photocopied signatures.
If the facility will hold resident cash, determine the maximum amount it expects to hold at one time and enter that amount on the LIC 400.
Contact a licensed surety company or agent and request a bond on the LIC 402 form in the amount stated on the LIC 400.
When the bond is issued, check that it uses the LIC 402 language, names the State of California as beneficiary, and shows effective and expiration dates.
Check that the bond carries the original seal and original signatures of the surety and the licensee, and that its amount matches the LIC 400 exactly. Return it to the surety for correction if not.
Calendar the bond expiration date and renew it before it lapses. The administrator sends a copy of the renewal to the licensing agency as the agency instructs.
If the facility holds resident cash, open a separate bank account titled as the residents' money. Do not deposit facility funds into it or withdraw resident money for facility use.
For each deposit or withdrawal, give the resident or representative a written receipt, keep a copy, and enter the transaction in the individual resident ledger the same day.
The administrator reconciles the resident account to the individual ledgers monthly and signs the reconciliation. A second person reviews it.
Give each resident or representative a statement of the account at least quarterly and on request.
If the amount held will rise above the bond amount, increase the bond and update the LIC 400 before accepting the additional money.
If the decision changes, the administrator notifies the licensing agency and amends the LIC 400 and LIC 402 as needed before the facility begins holding cash.
Include LIC 400 and LIC 402 in the final packet review (FC-01) with the bond amount and LIC 400 amount compared side by side.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether resident cash will be held, signs the LIC 400 and LIC 402, and pays for the bond.
Obtains the bond, tracks its expiration, maintains the separate resident account and records, and performs monthly reconciliations.
Independently reviews monthly reconciliations and confirms the bond amount matches the LIC 400.

documentation: Signed LIC 400 affidavit
Original LIC 402 surety bond with effective and expiration dates
Governing body decision on holding resident cash
Separate resident account statements, receipts, individual ledgers and monthly reconciliations
Bond renewal records

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Financial Forms and Start-Up Funds Verification (LIC 401, 401a, 403, 403a, 404)
policies.applies_to: Licensee/applicants, administrator, accountant or other financial preparer, and the reviewer of the application packet
policies.purpose: To demonstrate to CDSS that [AGENCY NAME] has the financial ability to open and operate the RCFE, by completing the required financial forms accurately and having start-up funds verified directly by the financial institution.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will complete all financial forms required by LIC 281, Section A, using realistic figures, and will keep approximately three months of operating funds available. This policy meets LIC 281 item A7 (LIC 401, Monthly Operating Statement): the number of residents corresponds to the requested capacity; income is clear and documented; costs are reasonable and salaries are at least minimum wage; approximately 25 percent of salaries is added for fringe benefits (or the reason it is not is explained); rent matches the lease, rental or mortgage payment; a separate LIC 401 is filed for each other licensed facility; the form states whether figures are estimated or actual; and the preparer's name and original signatures appear. This policy meets LIC 281 item A8(a) (LIC 401a, Supplemental Financial Information): Part I (other income and expenses, excluding facility income) is completed by individual applicants and each general partner, Part II is completed by all applicants, and the preparer's name and original signature appear. This policy meets LIC 281 item A8(b) (LIC 403, Balance Sheet): the LIC 403a is completed first; assets and liabilities of all owner activities are shown; figures are realistic; life insurance is shown at cash/surrender value; real estate is shown according to applicant type; on-site furnishings and equipment are at market value; only cash and cash equivalents count toward the three-month start-up funds; and preparer name and original signatures appear. This policy meets LIC 281 item A8(c) (LIC 403a, Balance Sheet Supplemental Schedule): it is a detailed balance sheet completed before the LIC 403, cash in the bank is verified with the LIC 404, liabilities are verified by credit report, and preparer name and original signatures appear. This policy meets LIC 281 item A9 (LIC 404, Financial Information Release and Verification): it is used to verify about three months of operating funds; a verifiable line of credit is acceptable if readily accessible; start-up funds are not spent on renovation or repair; the financial institution sends the verification directly to the licensing agency and the licensee does not hand-carry it; one form or set is used per bank; every person on an account signs; accounts are in the applicant's name; and signatures are originals.

definitions.definition: Cash and cash equivalents set aside to cover roughly three months of operating costs. They are not to be used for renovation or repair.
An asset that can be turned into cash immediately, such as a bank balance. Other assets do not count toward start-up funds.
Employer costs on top of salaries (for example payroll taxes and insurance), estimated at about 25 percent of salaries.
A verifiable credit facility that the applicant can readily access; it may be accepted in place of cash.

procedures: The administrator and financial preparer obtain the current LIC 401, 401a, 403, 403a and 404 forms and the LIC 281 instructions.
Prepare the staffing plan and budget first. Use the same capacity requested on the LIC 200 and the same positions and hours as the LIC 500 (see SA-04).
LIC 401: Enter the number of residents equal to the requested capacity and the expected resident income with its documentation.

LIC 401: List operating costs at reasonable amounts. Check that every salary is at least minimum wage and add about 25 percent of salaries for fringe benefits, or write a short explanation if fringe is not added.
LIC 401: Match rent or mortgage to the lease, rental or mortgage document. Mark each figure as estimated or actual. File a separate LIC 401 for any other licensed facility the applicant owns.
LIC 401a: Each individual applicant and each general partner completes Part I (non-facility income and expenses). All applicants complete Part II.

LIC 403a: Complete the detailed balance sheet schedule first, covering all owner activities. Show cash balances, which will be verified on the LIC 404, and liabilities, which will be checked against a credit report.

LIC 403: Carry totals from the LIC 403a. Show life insurance at cash/surrender value, real estate according to applicant type, and on-site furniture and equipment at market value. Use realistic figures.
Separate cash and cash equivalents from other assets and confirm cash and cash equivalents alone equal about three months of operating costs from the LIC 401.
LIC 404: Prepare one form or set for each bank. Every person named on the account signs in ink. Confirm the account is in the applicant's name, not a third party's.
If a line of credit will be used, confirm it is verifiable and readily accessible and list it on the LIC 404.
Send each LIC 404 to the financial institution for completion. Instruct the institution to send the verification directly to the licensing agency. Do not hand-carry or mail the verification yourself.

Do not spend start-up funds on renovation, repair or other pre-opening costs. Keep a record of account balances from signing through licensure and notify the licensing agency if balances fall below the verified amount.
Enter the preparer's name and original signature on every form. Applicants sign in ink; no photocopied signatures.
A second reviewer cross-checks LIC 401 against LIC 403/403a and LIC 404 for consistency and initials the checklist (FC-01).
Keep a copy of all financial forms in the confidential facility financial file and update them if circumstances change before licensure.

responsibilities.duty: Provide complete and truthful financial information, sign all forms, and keep start-up funds intact.
Prepares the forms in the required order, shows the preparer name, and signs.
Aligns the budget with the staffing plan and capacity, and coordinates the LIC 404 verification with each bank.
Checks forms against LIC 281 and each other before submission.

documentation: Signed LIC 401, 401a, 403, 403a and 404 forms
Lease, rental or mortgage documents supporting rent
Credit report supporting liabilities
Bank or line of credit documentation and record of balances
Reviewer checklist with date and initials

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Personnel Report and Staff Forms (LIC 500, 501, 503, 508)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee, hiring staff, and the reviewer of the application packet
policies.purpose: To submit accurate personnel forms showing that [AGENCY NAME] has planned sufficient, qualified, cleared and health-screened personnel to cover all hours of operation, as required by 22 CCR §87411 and §87355.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will complete the personnel forms required by LIC 281, Section A. This policy meets LIC 281 item A10 (LIC 500, Personnel Report): it shows all planned employee positions with days and hours of duty so required staff coverage can be checked for all hours of operation; lists the administrator and any staff already hired; lists unhired positions as 'to be hired' by position title; has the reverse side signed if there are fingerprint-exempt personnel; uses a separate LIC 500 for each other licensed facility; and has original signatures. This policy meets LIC 281 item A11 (LIC 501, Personnel Record): it is submitted with the application only for directors or administrators who are not licensees and who do not complete an LIC 215; other staff forms are kept on file at the facility. This policy meets LIC 281 item A12 (LIC 503, Health Screening Report - Facility Personnel): one form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator; the screening is less than six months old at the time of application; it is signed and dated by a qualified medical professional with no photocopied signatures; and the TB test portion is completed with the result, or a separate test verification is attached. This policy meets LIC 281 item A13 (LIC 508, Criminal Record Statement): one form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator. Under 22 CCR §87411, personnel must be sufficient in number and competent, anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older, residents may not substitute for required staff, volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan, and each staff member needs a physician health screening within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Under 22 CCR §87355 and §87411, DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, an exemption, or a transfer must be in place before any person works or is present in the facility.

definitions.definition: Persons who do not need fingerprint clearance under the rules. They are identified and the reverse of the LIC 500 is signed for them.
DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, exemption or transfer required before a person works or is present in the facility.
The physician or other licensed professional who signs and dates the LIC 503 health screening.
The entry used on the LIC 500 for planned positions not yet filled, listed by position title.

procedures: The administrator prepares a staffing plan showing every position by title and the days and hours each is scheduled so all hours of operation are covered (see ST-01).

Enter the plan on the LIC 500. List the administrator by name and any staff already hired. List all other positions as 'to be hired' with the position title. Do not count volunteers or residents toward required coverage.
Check that every person who will supervise staff or residents will be 18 or older.
If any personnel are fingerprint-exempt, identify them and sign the reverse side of the LIC 500. If the applicant owns other licensed facilities, prepare a separate LIC 500 for each.
Sign the LIC 500 in ink. Staffing hours on the LIC 500 must match the budget in the LIC 401 (see SA-03).

LIC 501: Determine whether the administrator or director is a non-licensee who does not complete a LIC 215. If so, have that person complete and sign the LIC 501 and include it with the application. Keep LIC 501s for all other staff in their personnel files at the facility.
LIC 503: Schedule the applicant or designee and the administrator for a health screening with a physician or other qualified medical professional.

Give the examiner the LIC 503. Make sure the TB test result is entered on the form, or attach a separate test verification. The screening must be less than six months old when the application is submitted.
Check that the professional signed and dated the LIC 503 in ink. Do not accept a photocopied signature.
LIC 508: Each of the applicant or designee and the administrator completes and signs one Criminal Record Statement in ink.
Complete fingerprinting for each person who needs it and do not allow anyone to work or be present until clearance, exemption or transfer is on file (see ST-02).
Compare the names, dates and titles across LIC 500, 501, 503, 508, LIC 308 and the administrator certification records so they are consistent (see SB-02).
After licensure, each new employee will have a health screening within 6 months before or 7 days after hire and criminal record clearance before starting work (see ST-02, ST-04).
The second reviewer checks the personnel forms against LIC 281 and initials the checklist (FC-01). File copies in the facility license file.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares the LIC 500 staffing plan, collects the personnel forms and ensures health screening and clearance before anyone works.
Completes and signs the LIC 503 and LIC 508 and verifies that the staffing plan is funded.
Completes, signs and dates the LIC 503 and records the TB result.
Verifies completeness and consistency before submission.

documentation: Signed LIC 500 Personnel Report (and reverse side if applicable)
LIC 501 for non-licensee directors or administrators, and other LIC 501s in staff files
LIC 503 Health Screening Reports with TB result or test verification
LIC 508 Criminal Record Statements
Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer records
Application checklist with reviewer initials

policies.category: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
policies.title: Emergency Disaster Plan, Facility Sketch and Fire Inspection Forms (LIC 610E, LIC 999, LIC 9054)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, maintenance staff and anyone preparing the emergency plan, facility sketch or fire clearance request
policies.purpose: To prepare the emergency disaster plan, facility sketch and fire inspection submissions required for the license application and to meet the plan content and fire clearance requirements of 22 CCR §87212 and §87202.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will submit a complete emergency disaster plan, a facility sketch and a fire inspection request with its application. This policy meets LIC 281 item A14 (LIC 610D; for RCFEs, LIC 610E, Emergency Disaster Plan): the plan shows two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate all residents, and if the applicant does not currently occupy the property, written authorization from the agency or person in possession of each relocation site is obtained and verified in writing. The plan will contain the elements required by 22 CCR §87212: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notification of a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers will be posted. This policy meets LIC 281 item A15 (LIC 999, Facility Sketch): the sketch shows dimensions and use of all rooms; door and window exits with exit routes numbered the same as on the LIC 610E; rooms for non-ambulatory residents and staff; all indoor and outdoor space including driveways, fences, storage, gardens and recreation areas; one sketch per building plus an overall sketch for multi-building sites; and, for the outdoor sketch, dimensions and the location of major equipment, swimming pools and utility shut-offs. This policy meets LIC 281 item A16 (LIC 9054, Fire Inspection), which the Section A table lists as 'Required' for an RCFE. Under 22 CCR §87202, fire clearance is required before licensure, and a separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. No fire inspection fee may be charged for homes of six or fewer beds. Ongoing emergency preparedness and fire drills are governed by SP-05 and SP-06.

definitions.definition: A location away from the facility, equipped for safe temporary accommodation, where residents will go if the facility cannot be occupied.
The predetermined place where residents and staff gather after leaving the building.
Approval from the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal that the facility meets fire safety requirements for its intended residents.
Unable to walk or move without the help of another person or a device; these residents require a separate fire clearance.

procedures: The administrator obtains the current LIC 610E, LIC 999 and the LIC 9054 fire inspection request and assigns responsibility for each.
Identify two relocation sites away from the facility that can hold all residents and provide safe temporary accommodation. List address, contact person and phone for each.
If the applicant does not yet occupy the property, obtain written authorization from the agency or person in possession of each relocation site and attach it to the LIC 610E.

Complete the LIC 610E with the elements required by 22 CCR §87212: administrative authority and staff assignments, fire safety plan, exits, assembly site, transportation, relocation sites, supervision and contact after relocation, and contacts with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies.
Include a step stating that the administrator or designee will notify each affected resident's hospice agency on any evacuation or relocation (see HS-06).
Number each exit route on the LIC 610E and make sure the numbers will match the LIC 999.

LIC 999: Draw each floor to scale or with dimensions, labeling every room by use. Mark all door and window exits, keyed by number to the LIC 610E routes. Identify rooms for non-ambulatory residents and for staff.
Prepare the outdoor sketch showing dimensions, driveways, fences, storage, gardens, recreation areas, major equipment, any swimming pool, and utility shut-off locations.
For a multi-building site, prepare one sketch per building and one overall sketch.
Walk the property with the sketch to verify accuracy and correct any differences before signing.
LIC 9054: Request fire inspection from the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal. If the home has six or fewer beds, do not pay a fire inspection fee.

State on the request whether non-ambulatory or bedridden residents will be accepted. If so, obtain the separate fire clearance required for them before admitting or keeping any such resident (see AD-03).
Make any corrections required by the fire authority and obtain the fire clearance before licensure. Attach or submit it as the licensing agency directs.
Post the emergency exit plans and emergency telephone numbers where staff and residents can see them. Keep the plan readily available to all staff.
Train all staff on the plan during orientation and review it at least annually or when the building, sites or contacts change (see SP-05, SP-06).
The second reviewer checks that the LIC 610E, LIC 999 and fire clearance are consistent and initials the checklist (FC-01).

responsibilities.duty: Completes the plan and sketch, arranges the fire inspection, posts exit plans and phone numbers, and trains staff.
Signs the plan, secures written authorization for relocation sites, and funds corrections required by the fire authority.
Helps measure and verify the sketch and identifies utility shut-off locations.

responsibilities.role: Local Fire Authority / State Fire Marshal
responsibilities.duty: Inspects the facility and issues the fire clearance.

documentation: Completed LIC 610E Emergency Disaster Plan
Written authorizations for each relocation site
LIC 999 facility sketches (indoor, outdoor and overall for multi-building sites)
LIC 9054 fire inspection request and fire clearance, including any clearance for non-ambulatory or bedridden residents
Records of posted exit plans and telephone numbers
Staff training sign-in sheets on the disaster plan

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Legal Entity Documents and Authority to Act (Partnership, Corporation, LLC)
policies.applies_to: Licensee, partners, corporate officers and directors, LLC managers and members, administrator, and the reviewer of the application packet
policies.purpose: To give the licensing agency the legal documents showing what type of entity [AGENCY NAME] is, who is ultimately responsible for which functions in the facility, and who has authority to sign and act on its behalf.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will submit the legal entity documents that match its form of ownership. This policy meets LIC 281 item B1 (Partnership Agreement / Articles of Incorporation / Articles of Organization), which is required for an RCFE because it tells the licensing agency who is ultimately responsible for which functions in the facility. For a partnership: this policy meets item B1.P1, a written partnership agreement is not necessary when the partners are husband and wife, and two individuals not related by marriage provide one; item B1.P2, [AGENCY NAME] determines whether the partnership is general or limited, and for a limited partnership only the general partner(s) are on the license but the names and addresses of limited partners are also provided; item B1.P3, all general partners are on the license and sign the application, with the name and business address of each; and item B1.P4, a description of the obligations and duties of each general partner and whether each can act on behalf of the others. For a corporation: this policy meets item B1.C1, Articles of Incorporation establishing a valid corporation qualified to do business in California, with the seal of the state of incorporation attached, and for a foreign (out-of-state) corporation a Certificate of Qualification from the California Secretary of State; item B1.C2, the constitution and by-laws governing day-to-day operation; item B1.C3, a Board Resolution identifying the agents acting for the corporation, including authorization to apply for a license and the person authorized to sign and act on its behalf; and item B1.C4, directors' and officers' names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers, and the name and address of each 10 percent shareholder. For a limited liability company: this policy meets item B1.L1, Articles of Organization stamped by the Secretary of State, and for a foreign LLC Secretary of State Form LLC-5 stamped by the California Secretary of State; and item B1.L2, the operating agreement and the names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers of all managing members, managers, and non-managing members holding a 10 percent or more interest, with a written delegation of authority consistent with the operating agreement if the signer is not identified in the operating agreement as having authority. Documents submitted will be consistent with the LIC 200 and LIC 309 (SA-01).

definitions.definition: A partner who is on the license, signs the application and is responsible for the facility; each general partner is an applicant.
A partner who is not on the license. Name and address are still provided to the licensing agency.
A written decision of a corporation's board naming the agents who may apply for the license and the person authorized to sign and act for it.
An entity organized outside California. It must also provide a California Secretary of State Certificate of Qualification (corporation) or stamped Form LLC-5 (LLC).
The document governing an LLC's management and its members' authority.

procedures: The licensee and administrator determine the entity type: individual, partnership, corporation, or LLC. Individual applicants do not need B1 entity documents beyond the forms in SA-01. The [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] records the entity type on the application checklist.

Partnership: Determine whether the partners are husband and wife. If so, a written partnership agreement is not necessary. If the partners are two individuals not related by marriage, obtain a signed written partnership agreement.

Partnership: Determine whether the partnership is general or limited. List each general partner with name and business address. Every general partner signs the application and is named on the license.
Partnership (limited): List the name and address of each limited partner. Only general partners appear on the license.
Partnership: Prepare a written description of the obligations and duties of each general partner and state whether each can act on behalf of the others. Each general partner signs it.

Corporation: Obtain Articles of Incorporation with the seal of the state of incorporation attached. If the corporation was organized outside California, also obtain a Certificate of Qualification from the California Secretary of State.
Corporation: Gather the constitution and by-laws that govern day-to-day operation.

Corporation: Hold a board meeting and adopt a Board Resolution that identifies the agents acting for the corporation, authorizes the license application, and names the person authorized to sign and act on its behalf. The secretary signs and dates it.
Corporation: Prepare a list of directors and officers with names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers, and the name and address of each 10 percent shareholder.
LLC: Obtain the Articles of Organization stamped by the Secretary of State. If the LLC is foreign, also obtain Form LLC-5 stamped by the California Secretary of State.

LLC: Gather the operating agreement and prepare a list of all managing members, managers and non-managing members holding a 10 percent or more interest, with names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers.

LLC: Check whether the operating agreement identifies the person who will sign the application as having authority. If it does not, prepare a written delegation of authority consistent with the operating agreement and attach it.
Compare the entity documents with the LIC 200, LIC 308 and LIC 309: names, titles, signers and terms of office must match (see SA-01).
Confirm that all copies are legible and that required seals and stamps are visible. Replace unclear copies.
The second reviewer checks each entity document against LIC 281 item B1 and initials the checklist (FC-01). File copies in the facility license file.
After licensure, the administrator updates the documents and notifies the licensing agency when partners, officers, managers, or authorized signers change (see GOV-01, GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts required resolutions and delegations, signs the entity documents, and keeps ownership information accurate.
Assembles the entity documents, tracks required seals and stamps, and notifies the licensing agency of changes.
Certifies resolutions and maintains the bylaws, operating agreement and ownership lists.
Checks the documents for completeness and consistency with the LIC 200 and LIC 309 before submission.

documentation: Partnership agreement (if required), general/limited partner list and duties statement
Articles of Incorporation with seal, Certificate of Qualification (foreign corporations), constitution and by-laws, Board Resolution, and list of directors, officers and 10 percent shareholders
Stamped Articles of Organization, stamped Form LLC-5 (foreign LLCs), operating agreement, member and manager list, and written delegation of authority if needed
Application checklist with reviewer initials and date

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Administrator Qualifications and Certification Verification
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designated substitute administrator, and Human Resources designee
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who serves as Administrator of [AGENCY NAME] meets the age, education, experience, good-character and certification requirements for a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) in California. The policy also sets out how those qualifications are documented and verified for the Department of Social Services (CDSS) before licensure and afterward.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will employ or designate only an Administrator who is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma or equivalent, is of good character, and holds a current RCFE administrator certificate (22 CCR §87405). The Administrator will be on the premises enough hours to manage the facility. A qualified substitute will be designated for any absence (22 CCR §87405). If the licensed capacity is 16 or more beds, the added education and experience requirements in §87405 will also be met.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B2.1 (Verification of Administrator Qualifications). LIC 281 B2 refers to a 40-hour certification program. Current law, HSC §1569.616, requires an 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and passage of the state exam within the statutory 60-day period. [AGENCY NAME] follows the statute and confirms the requirement with the CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau at 916-653-9300. Proof of registration in a certification program from an approved vendor is submitted with the application. A Department-issued certificate showing completion by an approved vendor is obtained before licensure.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B2.2 (Education). Transcripts from an accredited school are submitted when required. For schools outside the United States, [AGENCY NAME] submits class descriptions or a college catalog, or certification of class equivalency from a local college.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B2.3 (Experience). [AGENCY NAME] obtains written references stating that the person worked there, in what capacity, the specific duties and the period of employment. If a reference cannot be obtained, the Administrator signs a declaration stating why and giving the same details.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B2.4. Verification of experience is not needed when the application is for a one-to-six bed RCFE. If [AGENCY NAME] is licensed for seven or more beds, experience verification under B2.3 will be submitted.

definitions.definition: The individual designated by the licensee who is responsible for day-to-day operation of the facility and who holds a current RCFE administrator certificate.
The CDSS-approved initial program for RCFE administrators of 80 hours, at least 60 of them live, followed by the state exam.
A training provider approved by the CDSS Administrator Certification Bureau.
A qualified person named in writing to act as Administrator when the Administrator is absent.

procedures: Before hiring or designating an Administrator, the Licensee collects the candidate's government ID, date of birth, high school diploma or equivalent, and any transcripts, and confirms the candidate is 21 or older. The Licensee records the review in the Administrator Qualification File.
The Licensee checks that the candidate has good character. This means reviewing criminal record clearance or exemption status and professional references, and confirming no prior license revocation.

If the candidate is not yet certified, the Licensee enrolls the candidate in an approved-vendor 80-hour RCFE certification program (at least 60 hours live) and keeps the registration confirmation. The registration is submitted with the license application (B2.1).
The Licensee calls the Administrator Certification Bureau (916-653-9300) to confirm current program, exam and fee requirements, and records the call date and name of the person spoken to.
The candidate sits for the state exam within the 60-day period set by HSC §1569.616. The Licensee tracks the deadline on a calendar and diarizes a reminder at 30 days.

On passing the exam, the Administrator provides the Department-issued certificate. The Licensee confirms the certificate is from an approved vendor and puts a copy in the file. [AGENCY NAME] will not accept a resident before this certificate is in hand.

For education (B2.2), the Licensee requests transcripts from an accredited school when the position or capacity requires them. For foreign schools, the Licensee obtains class descriptions, a catalog, or a local-college equivalency letter.

For experience (B2.3), when the facility has seven or more beds or the Administrator's qualification depends on experience, the Licensee requests written references on the employer's letterhead. Each reference states that the person worked there, the capacity, specific duties and the dates.

If a reference cannot be obtained (for example, the employer closed), the Administrator completes and signs a declaration giving the reason and the same details. The Licensee attaches the declaration to the application (B2.3).
For a one-to-six bed RCFE, the Licensee notes in the file that experience verification is not required (B2.4), and keeps the Administrator's resume on file.
If the licensed capacity is 16 or more beds, the Licensee verifies the added education and experience in 22 CCR §87405 and keeps the documents.

The Licensee writes the Administrator's scheduled premises hours into the Plan of Operation and the staff schedule (see ST-01). The Licensee names a qualified substitute who is at least 21 with a current certificate or who meets the regulatory standard, and records the substitute in the file.

The Licensee tracks the Administrator's 40 hours of continuing education every two years, including 8 hours on dementia (HSC §1569.616). CE certificates go in the file, and a reminder is set six months before the certificate renewal date.

Before submitting the application, the Licensee uses the FC-01 checklist to confirm that the registration proof or certificate, education documents and experience documents (or declaration) are present.

The Licensee re-verifies each Administrator file annually as part of the GOV-03 quality review, and whenever the Administrator or substitute changes. The Licensee notifies CDSS of an Administrator change as required (see REC-02).

responsibilities.duty: Designates only a qualified Administrator and substitute. Verifies and files all qualification documents. Ensures certification and CE stay current.
Provides complete education, experience and certification records. Completes the 80-hour program, state exam and 40 hours of CE every two years. Keeps premises hours.
Meets the qualification standard and acts as Administrator during documented absences.
Maintains the Administrator Qualification File and CE calendar, and prepares the B2 portion of the application.

Proof of registration in an approved-vendor certification program (with application)
Department-issued administrator certificate and state exam results
Written experience references or a signed Administrator declaration (when required)
Record of call to the Administrator Certification Bureau (916-653-9300)
Continuing education certificates (40 hours every 2 years, including 8 hours dementia)
Written designation of substitute administrator and premises-hours schedule

policies.category: Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
policies.title: Job Descriptions and Personnel Policies
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, all employees and volunteers
policies.purpose: To define every staff position at [AGENCY NAME]. The policy states each position's duties, minimum qualifications and lines of supervision. It also sets personnel policies on work hours, abuse reporting, hiring conditions, and wages and leave so that competent staff cover the facility 24 hours a day.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will keep a written job description for every staff classification, and the descriptions will match the positions listed on the LIC 500 and on every personnel report (LIC 281 B4; B4.1). Personnel will be sufficient in number and competent for the care of residents. Anyone supervising staff or residents will be at least 18 years old. Residents will not substitute for required staff. Volunteers will be supervised and will not be counted in the staffing plan (22 CCR §87411).

This policy meets LIC 281 item B4.1 (a job description for each classification on the LIC 500). Classifications are: Administrator (including the designated substitute), Direct Care Staff / Caregiver, Awake Night Caregiver, Cook / Dietary Aide, Housekeeping and Laundry Aide, Maintenance Person, and Activity Coordinator [ADJUST TO MATCH THE LIC 500].

This policy meets LIC 281 item B4.2 (duties and responsibilities), item B4.3 (minimum qualifications corresponding to licensing requirements, including any special licenses, certificates or skills) and item B4.4 (lines of supervision, given and received). Each job description states all three. The Administrator job description requires certification, the age and education in 22 CCR §87405, scheduled premises hours and a designated qualified substitute. The Awake Night Caregiver job description sets out the duties of the awake night shift, including rounds, response to resident calls, medication assistance if trained, emergency response and evacuation duties, and who is called when problems arise.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B5.1 (work hours and shifts). The staff schedule shows the positions, work days and hours that give 24-hour coverage with competent staff, and it matches the LIC 500 and all personnel reports. See ST-01.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B5.2 (abuse reporting procedures). Each employee is told in writing, at hire and yearly, that as a care custodian they are a mandated reporter of elder and dependent adult abuse (W&I Code §15630). They must report to the licensing agency (CDSS), to law enforcement, and to the adult protective services or ombudsman agency. Reports are made by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible and followed by a written report (SOC 341) within the statutory time. See SP-01.

This policy meets LIC 281 item B5.3 (hiring practices). [AGENCY NAME] screens each applicant for the education and experience the job requires. Employees are told in writing that conditions of employment are fingerprint clearance, a statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, a physical examination or health questionnaire, and a child abuse index check. [AGENCY NAME] will pay at least the state minimum wage ($16.90 per hour in 2026) or any higher local minimum, and will provide at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year (Labor Code §246). Sole-caregiver meal and rest period rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly under IWC Wage Order 5 will be followed. Live-in and 24-hour shifts will be set up only after review by employment counsel.

definitions.definition: A staff position title with its own duties and qualifications, such as Direct Care Staff or Cook.
The Personnel Report listing each person who works in the facility, with position, days and hours.
A care custodian or facility employee required by law to report known or suspected elder or dependent adult abuse.
Staff who assist residents with personal activities of daily living.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the Administrator lists every position that will appear on the LIC 500 and writes a job description for each, using the [AGENCY NAME] job description template.

Each job description states: title; purpose of the position; duties and responsibilities (B4.2); minimum age, education, experience, and any license, certificate or skill needed, tied to licensing requirements (B4.3); supervisor's title; and positions supervised (B4.4).

For direct care staff, the minimum qualifications state: age 18 or older, completion of initial training and first aid (see SB-04), medication assistance training if the position assists with medications, TB screening, and criminal record clearance before starting work (22 CCR §87411).

The Administrator writes a separate Awake Night Caregiver duty statement covering rounds, response to call systems, medication assistance if trained, emergencies, evacuation and incident reporting. It states that the person remains awake and on duty throughout the shift.
The Administrator job description includes premises hours, responsibility for supervision of all staff and the designated substitute (22 CCR §87405). See SB-02.
The Administrator compares all job descriptions with the LIC 500 and any other personnel reports and corrects mismatches in title or hours before submission.

The Administrator prepares the staff schedule showing shifts, work days and hours with 24-hour competent coverage (B5.1). Schedules and the Plan of Operation are updated together whenever positions or hours change.

At hire, each employee receives a written statement of abuse-reporting duties (B5.2) naming CDSS, local law enforcement and adult protective services / the ombudsman, and the immediate-phone-then-written (SOC 341) requirement. The employee signs and dates a copy that goes in the personnel file.
The Administrator repeats the abuse-reporting notice at annual training and posts the reporting telephone numbers where staff can see them. See SP-01.
During hiring, the Administrator screens each applicant's education and experience against the job description and records the result on the screening checklist.

Before an offer becomes final, the Administrator gives the applicant the written conditions of employment (B5.3): fingerprint clearance, criminal conviction statement, TB clearance, physical examination or health questionnaire, and child abuse index check. The applicant signs to acknowledge them.
No one works or is present in the facility before criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is on file (22 CCR §87411). See ST-02.

Payroll sets all rates at or above the state minimum wage ($16.90 per hour in 2026) or any higher local minimum, and tracks paid sick leave accrual of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year (Labor Code §246).
The Administrator works with employment counsel before any live-in or 24-hour shift is used, and applies the Wage Order 5 meal and rest rules to any sole-caregiver shift.
