The Administrator confirms that the facility holds a current fire clearance from the fire authority before licensure and obtains a separate fire clearance before accepting or keeping any nonambulatory or bedridden resident (22 CCR §87202; SA-05). The Administrator records the clearance date and conditions.

New staff, including night staff, are oriented on the plan before working alone, and review the plan at least annually. They sign an acknowledgment kept in the personnel record (ST-03; ST-05). Night staff hold current first-aid training (22 CCR §87415; ST-01).

The Administrator stocks and checks emergency supplies, including flashlights, first aid kit, drinking water, food, medications, resident records, contact lists and portable communication, on a schedule set in the plan. Checks are logged.

When an emergency occurs, the senior staff person on duty takes command, calls 9-1-1 as needed, activates the plan, and notifies the Administrator. The Administrator or designee notifies the licensing agency, local fire authority and local health officer within the times in SP-02, and notifies each responsible person.

After any evacuation, relocation, drill or real emergency, the Administrator holds a debriefing within 7 days, records what worked and what did not, and updates the plan. The plan is reviewed in full at least annually and whenever the building, residents' needs, sites or contacts change (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Writes, maintains, posts and tests the plan, assigns roles, keeps the fire clearance, arranges sites and transportation and makes required reports.
Approves the plan, provides resources and reviews annual evaluation.
Know the plan and their assignments, carry out evacuation and head counts and follow the chain of command.
Know the emergency plan, hold first-aid training and act as incident lead until the Administrator arrives.

documentation: Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610E) with annual review dates
Fire clearance and any separate clearance for nonambulatory or bedridden residents
Agreements or letters for the evacuation site, relocation site and transportation
Posted exit plans and emergency numbers (photo or checklist of posting locations)
Emergency supply check log
Staff plan orientation acknowledgments
Debriefing notes and plan updates

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
policies.applies_to: All staff and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME], the Administrator and maintenance personnel
policies.purpose: To keep residents safe from fire by maintaining required fire clearance, a safe building, clear exits and working safety equipment, and by training staff and testing evacuation through regular drills.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not operate or admit residents without fire clearance. Fire clearance is required before licensure, and a separate fire clearance is required before the facility accepts or keeps any nonambulatory or bedridden resident (22 CCR §87202). The facility follows the Department's fire safety, fire drill and fire extinguisher requirements and the directions of the local fire authority, and the Administrator confirms the current drill frequency and equipment requirements with the licensing analyst and fire authority and records them here: [REQUIRED FIRE DRILL FREQUENCY AND EXTINGUISHER REQUIREMENTS]. Exit routes are kept clear, emergency lighting is kept working and exit plans are posted. The facility is maintained in accordance with 22 CCR §87303, including heat of at least 68°F and hot water between 105 and 120°F. Where the Act exempts homes of six or fewer beds, no fire-inspection fee is charged for them. Fire drill logs are kept on file.

definitions.definition: Written approval by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal that the building meets fire safety requirements for the licensed use and resident capability.
A resident who cannot leave the building without another person's help or is confined to bed; separate fire clearance is required before such residents are accepted or kept.
A practice of the fire safety and evacuation plan, in which staff and residents move to safety as they would in a real fire.
The path from any room to a safe place outside the building.
Lights that turn on automatically or are available if normal power fails, so exits can be found and used.

procedures: Before the license application is complete, the Administrator requests the fire inspection from the local fire authority and obtains fire clearance (22 CCR §87202; SA-05). A copy is kept in the facility file and submitted as required.

Before accepting or keeping any nonambulatory or bedridden resident, the Administrator confirms that the facility holds a separate fire clearance covering such residents. If it does not, the resident is not admitted or retained and the Administrator begins the process in AD-03.
The Administrator posts the fire safety plan and exit diagrams in [POSTING LOCATIONS], with each room's exit routes marked, and keeps emergency telephone numbers posted next to the telephone.

Staff walk the building daily with the daily safety checklist, checking that exits, hallways and stairs are free from furniture, equipment, trash and other obstruction, and that doors open easily from inside without a key.

Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms, fire extinguishers, sprinklers (if installed) and emergency lighting are tested and inspected at the frequency required by the fire authority and manufacturer. The maintenance person records each test with date, result and corrective action.

The Administrator confirms the required fire drill frequency and extinguisher requirements with the licensing analyst and fire authority, writes them into this policy at the placeholder above, and sets the drill calendar accordingly.

Fire drills are held on all shifts, including during sleeping hours when night staff are on duty, and at varied times. Each drill is led by the Administrator or a trained staff member and tests the alarm, evacuation of all residents (including those who use mobility aids), head count at the assembly point and shutting doors.

Residents are given help and instruction suited to their ability. Residents with dementia are accompanied by staff, and the staff member in charge records which residents took part, which needed help and how long it took to evacuate.

Each drill is recorded in the fire drill log: date, time, shift, duration, participants, problems found and corrective actions. The Administrator reviews and signs each entry, and logs are kept on file for review by the licensing agency and fire authority.

Staff are trained on fire safety, use of extinguishers and evacuation at orientation before working alone and at least annually, including their assigned roles in the Emergency Disaster Plan (SP-05; ST-03).

In an actual fire, staff activate the alarm, call 9-1-1, remove residents from danger, close doors, evacuate to the assembly site, account for every resident by head count and meet the fire department. Staff do not re-enter the building.
After an actual fire or explosion, the Administrator reports to the fire authority and licensing agency as set out in SP-02 and notifies each responsible person.

The Administrator ensures the building is maintained in accordance with 22 CCR §87303, including heat of at least 68°F and hot water of 105 to 120°F, and arranges repairs for any fire safety deficiency promptly. Residents are protected from any hazard in the meantime.
The Administrator keeps portable heaters, open flames, extension cords and cooking and smoking hazards under control according to SP-08 and DL-03, and reports any problem to the owner for correction.
The Administrator does not charge a fire-inspection fee to residents. For homes of six or fewer beds, the facility does not pay the fire authority an inspection fee where the Act exempts the home.
The Administrator reviews the fire drill log and inspection records at least quarterly and reports findings to the governing body (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and keeps fire clearance (including the separate clearance when required), confirms drill and equipment requirements, schedules and leads drills, reviews logs and corrects deficiencies.
Tests and inspects alarms, lighting and extinguishers, keeps exits clear and records results.
Know exit routes and assignments, take part in drills, report hazards and respond to alarms.
Funds repairs and equipment needed to keep fire clearance and review quarterly results.

documentation: Fire clearance and any separate clearance for nonambulatory or bedridden residents
Fire drill log with Administrator signature
Daily safety checklist and alarm, lighting and extinguisher inspection records
Posted exit plan photographs or posting checklist
Fire safety training records
Corrective action and repair records
Quarterly review notes

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers and contractors of [AGENCY NAME], the Infection Control Lead and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To prevent and control the spread of infection among residents, staff and visitors through a written plan, a trained Infection Control Lead, staff training, staff health screening and prompt reporting of outbreaks.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written infection control plan (LIC 9282) as required by 22 CCR §87470. The plan names an Infection Control Lead who has been trained by a qualified professional and sets initial and ongoing staff training. We review the plan annually, after an outbreak declaration and whenever the licensing agency asks. Every staff member has a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test for tuberculosis) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment (22 CCR §87411). Outbreaks are reported within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer (22 CCR §87211). Where staff may be exposed to blood or other potentially infectious materials, the facility follows the federal bloodborne pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, including an exposure control approach, protective equipment, sharps safety, hepatitis B vaccine offer and post-exposure follow-up.

definitions.definition: The facility's written plan under 22 CCR §87470 for preventing, detecting and responding to infections.
The staff member named in the plan who has been trained by a qualified professional and who oversees infection prevention and staff training.

An occurrence of infectious illness in more than the expected number of residents or staff, or as declared by the local health officer, that must be reported to licensing and the local health officer within 24 hours.
Basic infection prevention practices used with all residents: hand hygiene, gloves and other protective equipment, safe handling of sharps, cleaning and respiratory etiquette.
Microorganisms in human blood, such as hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, that can cause disease; regulated by 29 CFR 1910.1030.

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator completes the written infection control plan (LIC 9282) covering standard precautions, hand hygiene, personal protective equipment, cleaning and disinfection, laundry, food handling, waste, exposure incidents, outbreak response and visitor controls. The plan is approved by the owner.

The Administrator names the Infection Control Lead in the plan and arranges training for that person by a qualified professional (for example, a nurse, public health professional or infection preventionist). The training certificate or record is kept in the personnel file.

Staff receive initial infection control training at orientation before providing care, and ongoing training at least annually, as set in the plan. The training covers hand hygiene, personal protective equipment, standard precautions, cleaning, outbreak signs and reporting, and bloodborne pathogens (ST-03).

Each new staff member has a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after starting work, and the physician's documentation is kept in the personnel record (22 CCR §87411; ST-04; ST-05). Staff with symptoms of a contagious illness are sent home or kept from resident contact until cleared.

Staff wash hands before and after resident contact, before handling food or medications, after toileting care, and after removing gloves. Alcohol-based hand rub is available at [LOCATIONS]. Gloves and other protective equipment are used wherever there is a chance of contact with body fluids.

For bloodborne pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030), the Administrator identifies tasks that may expose staff to blood or other infectious material, provides gloves, gowns, eye protection, sharps containers and cleaning supplies at no cost to staff, offers the hepatitis B vaccine to staff with occupational exposure, and keeps training and vaccination records.

After a needlestick, splash or other exposure, the staff member washes the area, reports it to the Administrator immediately, and is sent for medical evaluation. The Administrator records the event and follow-up and keeps the records confidential (RR-06).

Housekeeping and laundry staff clean and disinfect high-touch surfaces daily and spills immediately using products approved for healthcare use, handle soiled linen with gloves and keep clean and soiled linen apart (DL-03).
Food is prepared and stored according to safe food handling practices, and staff with vomiting, diarrhea or open infected sores do not handle food (DL-01).

Staff watch residents for signs of infection such as fever, new cough, diarrhea, vomiting, rash, new confusion or wound changes. They report signs to the Administrator and nurse or physician consultant and, if indicated, move to isolation or contact precautions in the resident's room and notify the physician (HS-03).

Staff encourage and document residents' influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19 and other recommended vaccines according to physician advice and resident choice, respecting each resident's right to refuse (RR-01).

If two or more residents or staff have similar symptoms in a short time, or the local health officer declares an outbreak, the Infection Control Lead notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator calls or faxes the licensing agency and the local health officer within 24 hours (22 CCR §87211; SP-02) and records the time, method and person contacted.

During an outbreak, the Administrator follows the local health officer's instructions on isolation, cohorting, visitor limits, testing, staff exclusion and cleaning, notifies the responsible persons and keeps a line list of ill residents and staff.

The Administrator reviews the infection control plan at least annually, after any outbreak declaration, and whenever the licensing agency asks. The review is documented, and changes are made to the plan and training (GOV-03).
Staff dispose of regulated and medical waste, including sharps, according to the plan and local rules and keep sharps containers closed and out of reach of residents.
The Infection Control Lead reports infection trends and exposure incidents to the Administrator at least quarterly, and the Administrator reports them to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the plan, names and supports the Infection Control Lead, ensures training, screening and supplies, reports outbreaks and reviews the plan.
Completes qualified training, oversees prevention practices, trains staff, tracks infections and alerts the Administrator to outbreaks.
Follow standard precautions, use protective equipment, report symptoms and exposures and stay home when ill.
Provides outbreak direction and clinical guidance to the facility.

documentation: Infection control plan (LIC 9282) with annual review record
Infection Control Lead training record
Staff infection control and bloodborne pathogen training records
Staff physician screening documentation (chest x-ray or intradermal test)
Hepatitis B vaccine offer, acceptance or declination records
Exposure incident reports and follow-up
Outbreak line list, notification log and 24-hour report record
Cleaning logs and supply checks

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, residents, family members, visitors, ombudsmen, advocates and contractors at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set clear rules for smoking, visitors and animals that protect residents' personal rights and safety. The rules are stated in the plan of operation and the admission agreement, and they are consistent with the facility's fire safety and infection control policies.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] welcomes visitors and respects each resident's right to receive them. The visiting policy is stated in the plan of operation (22 CCR §87208) and in every admission agreement (22 CCR §87507). The firearms policy is also stated in every admission agreement (22 CCR §87507). Ombudsmen and resident advocates may visit residents privately at reasonable hours without prior notice (22 CCR §87468.1). The facility will not restrict a resident's visitors or associations because of actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status, and will use each resident's preferred name and pronouns (22 CCR §87468.1(b)). If the facility enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver, participants have access to visitors as required by the HCBS settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)). Smoking and pet rules are facility policy. They are set so they do not conflict with SP-06 (Fire Safety) or SP-07 (Infection Prevention and Control). Smoking is prohibited inside the building. Smoking is allowed only in the designated outdoor area, [DESIGNATED SMOKING AREA], which is away from entrances, windows and any oxygen storage or use. Firearms, other weapons and ammunition are not permitted on the premises, except for sworn peace officers acting in the line of duty. Facility-owned and visiting animals are permitted only under the conditions in the procedures below.

definitions.definition: Any person other than staff or a resident who enters the facility, including family, friends, clergy, volunteers and professionals invited by a resident.
A representative of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program or another resident advocate, who has the right to visit residents privately at reasonable hours without prior notice.

An animal individually trained to do work or perform tasks for a person with a disability. Service animals are handled under applicable disability-access law and are not treated as pets for purposes of this policy.
The outdoor location named in this policy where smoking is permitted. It is posted and kept free of combustible debris.

procedures: The Administrator states the visiting policy in writing in the plan of operation and in the admission agreement: visitors are welcome at reasonable hours, currently [VISITING HOURS], and residents may arrange other times with staff.

At admission, the Administrator or designee reviews the visiting policy and the firearms policy with the resident and representative. Both are written in the admission agreement, which is signed and dated within 7 days of admission and copied to the resident immediately.
Staff greet each visitor, ask them to sign the visitor log at the front entrance, and direct them to the resident. Staff do not interrogate visitors or require a reason for the visit.
A resident may ask that a visitor not be admitted. Staff honor the request, record it in the resident's record, and notify the Administrator.

Ombudsmen and advocates may visit residents privately at reasonable hours without prior notice. Staff direct them to the resident, provide a private space, and do not listen in, require an appointment, or inspect their materials.

Staff do not limit visitors, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, or association because of actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Staff use each resident's preferred name and pronouns.

If the facility enrolls in the Assisted Living Waiver, the Administrator ensures that waiver participants have access to visitors, with no restriction beyond what a participant's own documented preference or safety plan supports.

The Administrator may ask a visitor to leave, or limit a visit, only for a documented safety concern, such as threats, apparent intoxication, suspected abuse or exploitation, or an infection-control restriction. The Administrator records the reason on an incident report (SP-02) and reports any suspected abuse under SP-01.
Smoking rules are posted at the entrance and in the admission agreement. Smoking is prohibited indoors, including resident rooms. Staff do not smoke in resident areas.

Residents who smoke are identified at pre-admission screening (AD-01). The Needs and Services Plan (AD-02) records whether the resident needs supervision to smoke safely. Staff provide supervision when the plan requires it.
Matches and lighters for residents who cannot use them safely are held by staff. Ashtray receptacles at the smoking area are metal, non-combustible and emptied daily into a metal container.
No smoking occurs within [DISTANCE] feet of oxygen storage or use. 'No Smoking – Oxygen in Use' signs are posted wherever oxygen is stored or used.

Firearms, other weapons and ammunition are not permitted. A staff member who learns of one on the premises tells the Administrator right away. If there is an immediate danger, staff call 911 and follow SP-02.

Before a facility-owned animal is allowed, the Administrator confirms current vaccinations, a veterinary health check, a clean and healthy animal, and that no resident objects or has an allergy or fear. A staff member is assigned responsibility for the animal's care and waste removal.

A visiting animal is allowed with the Administrator's approval and proof of vaccination. It stays on a leash or in a carrier and out of the kitchen and food preparation areas. Staff clean and disinfect surfaces afterward as described in SP-07.
Animals are never left unsupervised with residents. Staff separate any animal that shows aggression and report any bite or scratch on an incident report within the same shift (SP-02).
The Administrator reviews this policy annually and after any smoking- or animal-related incident, and updates the plan of operation and admission agreement templates if needed (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Writes and maintains the visiting, firearms, smoking and pet rules. Includes them in the plan of operation and admission agreement, ensures ombudsman and advocate access, and decides any visitor restriction.
Welcome visitors, maintain the visitor log, supervise resident smoking when required, enforce smoking and weapon rules, and report incidents.
Keeps animal vaccination records current and manages the animal's care, waste removal and separation from residents when needed.
Follow the posted rules and tell staff of any concern about a visitor, smoke or an animal.

documentation: Visiting, firearms and smoking provisions in the signed admission agreement
Plan of operation visiting policy statement
Visitor log
Resident record notes on visitor preferences and restrictions
Needs and Services Plan entry on smoking supervision
Animal vaccination and health records
Incident reports for any visitor, smoking, weapon or animal event

policies.title: Food Service, Therapeutic Diets and Sample Menu
policies.applies_to: Dietary and kitchen staff, direct care staff, Administrator, residents and representatives at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To provide safe, nutritious, appealing meals and snacks that meet residents' needs and preferences. The policy also sets how therapeutic diets are ordered and served, and it contains the sample menu required with the license application.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] serves three meals and between-meal snacks every day, planned in advance, posted, and prepared and stored under the Title 22 food service requirements for RCFEs. This policy meets LIC 281, Section B10 (p. 18), Sample Menu, as follows. Item B10.1 (planned meals and snacks for one week, with foods from the four basic food groups): the one-week sample menu below includes every food group at each meal. Item B10.2 (portion sizes): portion sizes are listed below. Item B10.3 (times meals served): meal and snack times are listed below. Therapeutic diets are served only on a physician's order. If the facility enrolls in the Assisted Living Waiver, participants have access to food under the HCBS settings rule (42 CFR 441.301(c)): food and snacks are available at any time, and residents may choose among items.

MEAL TIMES: Breakfast 8:00 a.m.; mid-morning snack 10:00 a.m.; Lunch 12:00 noon; afternoon snack 3:00 p.m.; Dinner 5:30 p.m.; evening snack 8:00 p.m. Fluids and light snacks are available at any time.

PORTION SIZES (the four basic food groups): Milk and dairy: 1 cup milk or yogurt, or 1 oz cheese. Meat and protein: 2 to 3 oz cooked meat, poultry or fish; 1 egg; 1/2 cup cooked beans; 2 tablespoons peanut butter. Fruits and vegetables: 1/2 cup cooked or raw vegetable, 1/2 cup fruit or juice, or 1 medium piece of fruit. Breads and cereals: 1 slice bread, 1/2 cup cooked cereal, rice or pasta, or 1 cup dry cereal. Larger portions are offered on request.

ONE-WEEK SAMPLE MENU (substitutions of equal nutritional value are permitted and recorded):
Day 1 – Breakfast: oatmeal, scrambled egg, banana, toast, milk, coffee/tea. Snack: apple slices and cheese. Lunch: turkey sandwich on whole wheat, vegetable soup, fruit cup, milk. Snack: graham crackers and juice. Dinner: baked chicken, mashed potatoes, green beans, dinner roll, canned peaches, milk. Evening snack: yogurt.
Day 2 – Breakfast: bran flakes with milk, orange juice, hard-boiled egg, toast. Snack: pudding. Lunch: tuna salad on bread, tossed salad, applesauce, milk. Snack: crackers and cheese. Dinner: meatloaf, baked potato, steamed carrots, bread, fresh fruit, milk. Evening snack: banana.
Day 3 – Breakfast: pancakes with syrup, sausage, orange slices, milk. Snack: yogurt. Lunch: macaroni and cheese, peas, pear halves, bread, milk. Snack: juice and cookies. Dinner: baked fish, rice, broccoli, bread, melon, milk. Evening snack: cottage cheese and fruit.
Day 4 – Breakfast: cream of wheat, scrambled egg, toast, grapefruit juice, milk. Snack: banana. Lunch: chicken noodle soup, cheese sandwich, carrot sticks, fruit, milk. Snack: crackers and peanut butter. Dinner: beef stew with vegetables, biscuit, tossed salad, gelatin with fruit, milk. Evening snack: warm milk and cookies.
Day 5 – Breakfast: French toast, applesauce, bacon, milk, coffee/tea. Snack: orange wedges. Lunch: egg salad sandwich, tomato soup, green salad, fruit, milk. Snack: yogurt. Dinner: roast pork, sweet potato, spinach, bread, baked apple, milk. Evening snack: toast with jam.
Day 6 – Breakfast: cold cereal with milk, toast with peanut butter, banana, juice. Snack: cheese cubes and grapes. Lunch: beef and bean burrito, rice, shredded lettuce and tomato, fruit, milk. Snack: pudding. Dinner: spaghetti with meat sauce, green salad, garlic bread, fruit cocktail, milk. Evening snack: yogurt.
Day 7 – Breakfast: omelet with cheese, hash browns, toast, orange juice, milk. Snack: muffin and juice. Lunch: baked chicken, noodles, mixed vegetables, bread, pears, milk. Snack: fruit and crackers. Dinner: ham, scalloped potatoes, cabbage, roll, ice cream, milk. Evening snack: graham crackers and milk.

definitions.definition: Milk and dairy; meat and protein; fruits and vegetables; breads and cereals.
A diet ordered by a physician for a medical condition, such as diabetic, low-sodium, renal, mechanical-soft or pureed.
The one-week menu of planned meals and snacks submitted with the license application, showing the four food groups, portion sizes and meal times.
A change to a planned menu item for supply, preference or dietary reasons, replaced by an item of equal nutritional value.

procedures: The Administrator or designated cook plans menus at least one week ahead, using the sample menu as the baseline, and ensures each day includes foods from all four basic food groups. The menu is dated and posted where residents can see it.
Meals and snacks are served at the times stated above. If a resident misses a meal for any reason, staff offer a meal or substitute and record the reason.

At pre-admission screening (AD-01), staff record each resident's food preferences, allergies, cultural or religious dietary needs, chewing or swallowing problems and any physician-ordered diet. The results go into the Needs and Services Plan (AD-02).
A therapeutic diet is served only on a written physician order. The order is placed in the resident's record, and the Administrator or designee writes the diet on the kitchen diet list.
Kitchen staff are trained on each active therapeutic diet. The diet list is posted in the kitchen out of residents' view. Residents are not served a modified diet without a current order.

A resident who refuses a prescribed diet is counseled by staff, and the refusal is recorded. The Administrator notifies the physician and the representative if the refusal risks the resident's health (HS-03).
Staff cook, hold and serve food safely. Refrigerators are kept at 41°F or below and freezers at 0°F or below. Hot foods are held at 135°F or above. Temperature is checked and logged daily.

Staff store food off the floor in labeled, covered, dated containers. Cleaning supplies and chemicals are stored apart from food. Dishes, utensils and surfaces are washed and sanitized after each meal, and the kitchen is cleaned daily.
Staff who prepare or serve food wash hands, wear clean clothing and hair covering, and do not work with food while ill, in line with SP-07.

Staff help residents who need it with eating, offering assistive devices, proper positioning and enough time. Staff watch for choking, weight changes and poor intake, and report concerns to the Administrator under HS-03.
Safe drinking water and fluids are available to residents at all times. Healthy snacks are kept in an accessible area for residents between planned snacks.

If the facility enrolls in the Assisted Living Waiver, the Administrator ensures waiver participants can obtain food and snacks at any time and are offered choices at meals, in line with the HCBS settings rule.
Staff keep a record of any menu substitution on the posted menu. Menus as served are kept for at least 30 days.

The Administrator reviews the menu at least quarterly with residents or the resident council, seeks feedback on taste, variety and portions, and adjusts the menu accordingly. The Administrator also reviews this policy annually (GOV-03).
The Administrator keeps the sample menu with the license application packet (FC-01) so a reviewer can verify items B10.1, B10.2 and B10.3.

responsibilities.duty: Approves menus and the diet list, ensures physician orders are on file, monitors food quality and safety, and keeps the sample menu with the application.
Prepare menus per plan and portion standards, follow modified-diet orders, maintain food safety and cleaning logs, and record substitutions.
Serve meals, assist residents who need help eating, and report intake problems, choking, weight changes or food refusals.
Orders and updates therapeutic diets in writing.
Share food preferences, allergies and cultural needs and give feedback on menus.

documentation: One-week sample menu (LIC 281, B10) with portion sizes and meal times
Posted weekly menus and substitution records (kept at least 30 days)
Physician orders for therapeutic diets in resident records
Kitchen diet list
Daily refrigerator and freezer temperature logs
Kitchen cleaning log
Resident food preference and allergy information in the Needs and Services Plan

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
policies.applies_to: Activity staff, direct care staff, Administrator, residents and representatives at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To provide planned, meaningful activities that suit residents' abilities, interests and needs, encourage independence and community connection, and are tailored to each resident's appraisal and Needs and Services Plan.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides a planned activity program and follows the Title 22 requirements for planned activities and resident councils. The Administrator keeps a daily activity schedule and a monthly calendar stating who plans and who conducts each activity. Activities are tailored to resident appraisals and Needs and Services Plans. Participation is voluntary, and a resident's choice not to participate is respected. The facility's activity approach is part of the plan of operation (22 CCR §87208). If the facility advertises dementia special care, the activities component is included in the written dementia program required by 22 CCR §87706, and advertisements are kept for 3 years.

definitions.definition: A scheduled, staff- or volunteer-led event that offers social, physical, cognitive, creative or spiritual engagement.
A monthly calendar of planned activities, showing the time, name of the activity, and the person who plans and conducts it.
A group of residents who meet to discuss facility life and give suggestions, organized under the applicable Title 22 requirements.
The written program required of a facility that advertises dementia special care, which addresses activities among other topics.

procedures: At pre-admission screening and appraisal (AD-01), staff gather each resident's interests, life history, abilities, routines, cultural and spiritual preferences and sensory or mobility limits.
The Administrator or designee records activity preferences and any needed supports in the Needs and Services Plan (AD-02) and updates them at each reappraisal.

The Administrator designates an activity coordinator. The coordinator drafts a monthly calendar by the 25th of the preceding month, stating for each activity the time, place, and the person who plans and conducts it.

Each month's calendar offers a mix of activities, including physical exercise, social events, mental stimulation, creative arts, music, spiritual or cultural activities, and community outings where feasible.
A daily schedule is posted in a common area and read aloud or given to residents who cannot read it. Large-print copies are made available.
Staff invite each resident to activities and offer help getting there. Residents who stay in their rooms are offered one-to-one activities, such as conversation, reading, music, hand care or puzzles.
Activities for residents with dementia are short, simple, structured and adapted to ability. They follow HS-04, and staff redirect rather than correct or force participation.
Staff record each resident's attendance and level of participation on an activity log. Staff note refusals without penalty.
Volunteers who help with activities are supervised by staff, are not counted toward required staffing, and have required criminal record clearance before any presence (ST-02).
Any trip outside the facility follows DL-04 (Transportation) and the resident's right to leave and take part in community life.

The Administrator supports a resident council if residents wish to form one, provides a meeting space, and responds to suggestions in writing within a reasonable time. Staff do not attend council meetings unless invited by the residents.
If the facility advertises dementia care, the activities section of the written dementia program is kept current, and each advertisement is kept for 3 years.
The coordinator reviews attendance and resident feedback each quarter, drops activities that are not working, and reports the findings to the Administrator for quality assurance (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Assigns the activity coordinator, ensures the program matches the plan of operation and Needs and Services Plans, supports the resident council, and keeps dementia advertisements for 3 years.
Prepares the daily schedule and monthly calendar naming who plans and conducts each activity, leads or arranges activities, and keeps attendance logs.
Encourage and assist residents to take part, adapt activities to ability, and report changes in mood or participation.
May choose which activities to join and give suggestions directly or through the resident council.

documentation: Daily activity schedule
Monthly activity calendar naming who plans and conducts each activity
Activity attendance and participation log
Activity preferences in the Needs and Services Plan
Resident council meeting notes and responses, if a council is formed
Written dementia program (activities section) and dementia advertisements kept 3 years, if applicable

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: Housekeeping, laundry and maintenance staff, direct care staff, Administrator and contractors at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep the building, grounds, equipment and furnishings clean, safe, comfortable and in good repair, and to meet the state's standards for temperature, hot water, bedroom occupancy and bathroom fixtures.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps the facility clean, sanitary, free of hazards and in good repair. Heat is maintained at no less than 68°F, and hot water at resident-accessible fixtures is kept between 105°F and 120°F (22 CCR §87303). No more than 2 residents share a bedroom. The facility has at least 1 toilet and washbasin for every 6 persons and at least 1 tub or shower for every 10 persons, counting live-in staff and family members (22 CCR §87307). The plant is kept clean and in good repair, with grab bars, non-slip surfaces and emergency lighting. Any private water supply is tested, annually for a capacity of 7 to 15 (22 CCR §87303).

definitions.definition: Upkeep of the building, grounds, equipment, furniture and systems so they are safe, clean and in good repair.
The required number of toilets, washbasins and tubs or showers per number of people using them, counting live-in staff and family.
A well or other water source not provided by a public utility, which must be tested at required intervals.
Battery or backup lighting that comes on automatically when power fails, so people can exit safely.

procedures: The Administrator assigns daily and weekly cleaning tasks to named staff on a posted housekeeping schedule covering resident rooms, bathrooms, kitchen, common areas, hallways and entrances.

Housekeeping staff clean bathrooms and high-touch surfaces at least daily and as needed, using products and methods set out in SP-07. Chemicals are labeled, kept in original containers and stored locked, away from food and medications.

Staff check each bedroom to confirm no more than 2 residents are assigned. The Administrator checks the fixture count against the residents, live-in staff and family members in the home, and acts before a new admission if the ratio would be exceeded (1 toilet and washbasin per 6; 1 tub or shower per 10).

Staff check and record the indoor temperature in the morning and evening. The heat is kept at 68°F or higher. If it falls below, the Administrator arranges repair, provides blankets or safe supplemental warmth, and records the action.

Maintenance staff test water temperature at accessible hot water fixtures weekly with a thermometer and record the results. Water must be between 105°F and 120°F. Out-of-range water is reported to the Administrator immediately and repaired before use if above 120°F.

Staff inspect grab bars, handrails, non-slip floor and tub surfaces, lighting, flooring and furniture weekly and repair or remove anything unsafe. Residents are not exposed to hazards while a repair is pending.
Maintenance staff test emergency lighting monthly and replace batteries or bulbs as needed. Testing is recorded and tied to SP-05 and SP-06.

If the facility uses a private water supply and capacity is 7 to 15, the Administrator has the water tested annually by a certified laboratory and keeps the result on file (SB-07). A failed test triggers corrective action and retest, and the Administrator tells residents of any unsafe water.

Laundry is done at least weekly and as needed. Soiled or wet linens are handled with gloves, bagged at the point of use, and kept separate from clean linens. Linens are washed at hot-water temperature with detergent and dried completely.
Resident clothing is labeled and washed according to the resident's preferences, kept separate from facility linens, and returned to the right resident. Missing items are handled under RR-04.
Beds are changed at least weekly and whenever soiled. Mattresses and pillows are kept clean and in good repair, and replaced if soiled beyond cleaning.
The Administrator arranges pest control as needed and at least quarterly, using safe methods. Staff report signs of pests the same day.
Staff report repair needs on a maintenance request log. The Administrator prioritizes safety repairs, assigns the work, and records the completion date.
The Administrator walks through the facility monthly using a checklist and reports findings to the quality assurance review in GOV-03.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the building and grounds meet the standards in this policy, checks fixture ratios and occupancy, arranges repairs and water testing, and reviews logs.
Clean and sanitize as scheduled, handle linens safely, store chemicals securely, and report hazards.
Test temperatures and emergency lighting, inspect grab bars and surfaces, and complete repairs.
Report spills, hazards and repair needs immediately, and keep resident areas clean between scheduled housekeeping.

documentation: Housekeeping schedule and cleaning checklists
Indoor temperature log
Weekly hot water temperature log
Maintenance request and repair log
Emergency lighting test record
Water test results for any private water supply
Bedroom occupancy and bathroom fixture count
Monthly walk-through checklist

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: Drivers, direct care staff, Administrator, residents and representatives at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To describe how the facility arranges safe transportation, to ensure drivers are screened and trained, and to ensure transportation charges are disclosed in writing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] states its transportation arrangements in the plan of operation (22 CCR §87208). Transportation is provided for [DESCRIBE: medical appointments, outings and other trips, and by whom]. Any charge for transportation is listed as an additional service, with its rate, in the admission agreement (22 CCR §87507). Anyone who drives residents for the facility is staff and must have criminal record clearance or an exemption before working or being present (22 CCR §87355). Drivers also receive training as a facility practice, as set out below. Residents keep their right to leave the facility and take part in community activities, and the facility does not use transportation to restrict that right.

definitions.definition: Transport of residents in a facility-owned or staff vehicle, or by a contracted provider arranged by the facility.
A service beyond basic services that is listed separately with its rate in the admission agreement.
A staff member authorized by the Administrator to transport residents.
DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption required before a person works or is present at the facility.

procedures: The Administrator describes in the plan of operation who provides transportation, what vehicles are used, and which trips (such as medical appointments and outings) are covered, and updates it when arrangements change.

For each charge, the Administrator lists transportation in the admission agreement as an additional service with the rate and the basis (per trip or per mile). Charges are explained to the resident and representative before the agreement is signed. A change in rate follows the 60 days' written notice requirement in the admission agreement (RR-03).

Before any staff member drives residents, the Administrator confirms criminal record clearance or exemption (ST-02), a valid California driver license, a satisfactory driving record, and current auto insurance covering the transport.

Drivers receive an orientation before driving residents. It covers safe loading and unloading, wheelchair securement, seat belt use, assisting residents with mobility limits, emergency procedures, and the facility's first-aid training.

Vehicles are inspected before use and serviced regularly. The Administrator keeps maintenance and inspection records. Each vehicle carries a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher, a phone and a list of emergency contacts.
Before a trip, staff identify residents who need an escort, wheelchair securement, oxygen, medication on the trip or toileting help. The Needs and Services Plan guides these decisions.
Staff use seat belts and wheelchair tie-downs for every resident. Residents are not left alone in a vehicle. Drivers do not use phones while driving and do not smoke in the vehicle.
A staff member keeps a trip log with date, driver, vehicle, residents on board, destination, and departure and return times. Staff confirm every resident is accounted for before and after each trip.
Residents may decline a trip or arrange their own transport. Families may transport residents at their own choice. Staff record sign-out and return times for residents who leave with others.

If a resident is injured or becomes ill during a trip, the driver pulls over safely, calls 911 if needed, notifies the Administrator, and follows SP-02 and HS-03. The Administrator completes any required report.
If a resident on an outing is missing, the driver follows SP-03 immediately.
The Administrator reviews driver records, vehicle logs and trip logs quarterly, and corrects any gaps (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: States transportation in the plan of operation, lists charges in the admission agreement, authorizes drivers, and ensures clearance, insurance, vehicle upkeep and trip records.
Hold a valid license, maintain a safe driving record, complete orientation, inspect vehicles, secure residents, keep trip logs and report incidents.
Prepare residents, escort those who need help, and confirm every resident's return.
Request trips, understand the charges, and may arrange their own transportation.

documentation: Plan of operation transportation statement
Admission agreement showing transportation as an additional service with its rate
Driver clearance, license, driving record, insurance and orientation records
Vehicle maintenance and inspection records
Trip log and resident sign-out/return records
Incident reports for any transport-related event

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Night Supervision and Scheduling
policies.applies_to: Administrator, all direct care staff, scheduling staff, volunteers and substitutes at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure the facility always has enough competent staff, including overnight, to meet residents' needs and carry out emergency procedures, and to schedule staff in compliance with California rules.
policies.policy: California sets no numeric staff-to-resident ratio for RCFEs. [AGENCY NAME] keeps personnel sufficient in numbers and competent to meet residents' needs, as required by 22 CCR §87411. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need, and the facility will comply. Anyone who supervises staff or residents is 18 or older. Residents never substitute for required staff. Volunteers are supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan. Night supervision (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.) follows 22 CCR §87415. With fewer than 16 residents, a qualified person is on call on the premises overnight. With 16 to 100 residents, one employee is awake on duty and one is on call within 10 minutes. In a home with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person is awake and on duty whenever a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation (22 CCR §87705). Night staff know the emergency plan and are first-aid trained. The Administrator is on the premises a sufficient number of hours and designates a qualified substitute when absent (22 CCR §87405). Meal and rest periods are scheduled under IWC Wage Order 5, which has special rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. The facility obtains employment counsel before using live-in or 24-hour shifts.

definitions.definition: The number and competence of staff needed to meet the care and supervision needs shown by resident appraisals, Needs and Services Plans and observation.
10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
A staff member who is awake, dressed and alert, and able to respond immediately to residents.
A qualified person who sleeps or rests at the facility and is available to respond to residents at night.
A staff member who can reach the facility within 10 minutes when called (16-100 residents).
A person meeting Administrator qualifications who is designated to run the facility when the Administrator is absent.

procedures: The Administrator prepares a written staffing plan before opening and reviews it at every admission, reappraisal and change of condition. The plan shows required staff by shift based on the number of residents, their care needs and the building layout.

The Administrator uses appraisals (AD-01) and Needs and Services Plans (AD-02) to decide whether more staff are needed, for example for residents who need two-person transfers, frequent toileting, behavioral support or awake night supervision.

The Administrator keeps staffing at a level that lets staff provide all planned services, supervise residents, prepare meals, run drills and respond to emergencies at the same time. If a shift is short, the Administrator calls in additional staff before accepting a new admission.

The Administrator writes a weekly schedule, posts it at least 7 days ahead, and keeps all past schedules. The schedule shows each worker's name, position, and the hours worked, and identifies the Administrator, the on-call staff and the substitute.
No resident performs required staff duties. Volunteers are supervised by staff, are not counted in the staffing plan, and have required criminal record clearance before any presence (ST-02).
Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. The Administrator verifies age on the personnel file (ST-05).
The Administrator confirms every worker's clearance, TB/health screening, training and first aid card before placing them on a shift alone (ST-02, ST-03, ST-04).

Licensed capacity is [LICENSED CAPACITY]. For fewer than 16 residents, a qualified person who is on call and sleeps on the premises is scheduled every night. The schedule names that person and shows where they sleep.
If the census reaches 16 or more, the Administrator schedules one employee awake on duty plus one employee on call within 10 minutes for every night shift, before the 16th resident is admitted.

If appraisal, reappraisal or observation shows a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, the Administrator schedules a staff person awake and on duty throughout the night, records the decision in the resident's record, and updates the schedule the same day (HS-04).

Night staff are first-aid trained and are oriented to the emergency plan, evacuation routes, resident locations, medications on hand and who to call. Orientation is documented before the first solo night shift (SP-05, SP-06).

Night staff check residents at intervals set in each Needs and Services Plan and record unusual events on the shift log. They call the Administrator or on-call supervisor for any emergency and call 911 when necessary.

The Administrator is on the premises enough hours to oversee operations, and the schedule shows those hours. When the Administrator is absent, a qualified substitute is named on the schedule and knows how to reach the Administrator.

Before using any live-in, 24-hour or sole-caregiver shift, the Administrator gets written advice from employment counsel on Wage Order 5 meal and rest period requirements. The scheduling method adopted is recorded in the staffing plan.
Staff record meal and rest periods on time records. Any missed or interrupted period is recorded, and the Administrator takes corrective action and any required pay adjustments.
If a staff member calls out, the Administrator or on-call supervisor fills the shift from a list of qualified, cleared staff. Staff do not leave until relieved.

The Administrator reviews staffing monthly with the schedule, incident reports and complaints, and adds staff if documentation shows a need. If CDSS requires more staff, the Administrator implements the increase right away and records it (GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Writes and reviews the staffing plan, schedules qualified staff, ensures night supervision and awake staff when required, is on premises sufficient hours, names a qualified substitute and obtains employment counsel on live-in or 24-hour shifts.
Manages the facility while the Administrator is absent and meets Administrator qualifications.
Complete first aid and emergency plan orientation, remain on call or awake as scheduled, supervise residents and respond to emergencies.
Report as scheduled, record time and meal/rest periods, and tell the Administrator when staffing is not enough to meet resident needs.
Prepares and posts the weekly schedule, tracks cleared and trained staff, and maintains the call-out list.

documentation: Written staffing plan
Weekly schedules showing names, positions, hours, on-call and substitute
Night supervision schedule and any awake-night decision for residents with dementia
Time records, meal and rest period records
Night staff emergency plan orientation and first aid records
Administrator hours and substitute designation
Employment counsel advice on live-in or 24-hour shifts, if used

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Licensee/applicant, administrator, adult household members, all employees, and any other person who works at or is present in the facility
policies.purpose: To make sure that no one works or is present in [AGENCY NAME] without DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, a criminal record exemption, or an approved transfer of clearance, so residents are protected from harm and the facility meets California licensing requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance, a criminal record exemption, or a clearance transfer for the applicant, the administrator, every adult household member and every staff member before that person begins work or is present in the facility (22 CCR §87355; 22 CCR §87411). Every person also completes the criminal record statement, LIC 508. No one without clearance, exemption or transfer may be present in the facility or work alone with residents, and no resident may substitute for required staff. Volunteers who are present are covered by the same rule. Clearance records are kept in the personnel file. In addition, as facility practice, the agency verifies professional licenses and certifications and checks federal exclusion lists for people who will be involved in resident care or billing.

definitions.definition: Notice from the licensing agency that a person's DOJ and FBI fingerprint results permit the person to work or be present in a licensed facility.
Written approval from CDSS that allows a person with a criminal record to work or be present despite a conviction.
Moving an existing clearance or exemption to this facility through the process the licensing agency allows.
The Criminal Record Statement that each person completes and signs.
Working, volunteering, living in, or otherwise being on the premises other than as a resident or a visitor of a resident.

procedures: Before an offer of employment becomes final, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) tells the candidate that employment depends on fingerprint clearance, exemption or transfer and on a signed LIC 508.
The candidate completes and signs LIC 508 before the first day of work. The Administrator reviews it and places it in the personnel file.

The Administrator directs the candidate to complete the fingerprint submission to DOJ and FBI through the Live Scan process the licensing agency requires, using the facility's identifying information, and keeps the submission receipt.
If the candidate already holds a clearance or exemption, the Administrator starts the transfer process with the licensing agency and records the date of the request.
The Administrator verifies the clearance, exemption or transfer status from CDSS notification and does not accept a verbal statement from the candidate as proof.
Until written proof is on file, the person may not start work, be present in the facility, work alone with residents, or be counted in the staffing plan.
The same process applies to the applicant, the administrator and every adult living in the licensee's household before they are present in the facility.

The Administrator checks that each volunteer, contractor or other adult who will be in the facility without a resident's visitor status has clearance before access is given, or ensures the person is never left unsupervised only if the licensing agency allows it.
The Administrator places a copy of the clearance, exemption or transfer notice, the LIC 508, and the fingerprint receipt in the personnel file and notes the date on the personnel record (LIC 501).

As facility practice, the Administrator verifies any professional license or certification that a position requires (for example, nursing or administrator certificates) with the issuing agency and records the verification date.

As facility practice, if the facility participates in the Assisted Living Waiver or any other government payment program, the Administrator checks applicable federal and state exclusion lists before hire and at least annually, and records the results.

If the licensing agency notifies the facility that a person's clearance is denied, revoked or requires an exemption, the Administrator removes the person from work immediately, documents the date and time, and follows the licensing agency's instructions.
The Administrator reports any new arrest or conviction information received about a staff member to the licensing agency as required and keeps the correspondence in the file.
Each quarter the Administrator audits all personnel files against the staff roster and records the audit date, findings and corrections.
Staff who learn that a co-worker or volunteer is working without clearance report it immediately to the Administrator.

responsibilities.duty: Confirms clearance before anyone works or is present, keeps the records, performs audits, and removes anyone without valid clearance.
Ensures the licensee, board members or household members who are present in the facility have clearance, and supports enforcement of this policy.
Complete LIC 508 and fingerprinting truthfully and on time, and notify the Administrator of any new criminal history.
Does not schedule anyone not listed as cleared by the Administrator.

documentation: LIC 508 Criminal Record Statement for each person
Fingerprint submission receipt
Clearance, exemption or transfer notice from the licensing agency
Registry, exclusion list and license verification records
Quarterly personnel file audit log
Personnel record (LIC 501) showing the clearance date

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: Administrator, direct care staff, staff who assist with medications, and all personnel who supervise or care for residents
policies.purpose: To make sure that every person hired by [AGENCY NAME] is qualified, oriented and trained before and during the work, as required by the Health and Safety Code and Title 22, so residents receive competent care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs enough competent personnel to meet resident needs (22 CCR §87411). Anyone who supervises staff or residents is at least 18 years old. Direct care staff receive 40 hours of initial training under HSC §1569.625: the first 20 hours are completed before the person works alone and include 6 hours on dementia and 4 hours on postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. The second 20 hours, which include 6 more hours on dementia (a total of 12 hours of initial dementia training under HSC §1569.626), are completed within 4 weeks. Every direct care staff member then completes 20 hours of training each year, including 8 hours on dementia. Staff who assist with medications complete medication assistance training under HSC §1569.69. Care staff hold first aid training from a qualified provider. The administrator holds a current certificate under HSC §1569.616. Training documentation is kept in the personnel record.

definitions.definition: Employees who assist residents with personal activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, eating, toileting and mobility.
Practical, supervised instruction in which the trainee demonstrates the skill, not only classroom or reading instruction.
Hours of approved training that a certified administrator must complete to renew the administrator certificate.
A first aid trainer whose course meets the licensing agency's requirements, with a card or certificate issued to the staff member.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) uses the written job description (SB-03) to screen candidates, confirms the candidate is 18 or older, and confirms clearance under ST-02 and health screening under ST-04 before the first shift.

On or before the first day, the Administrator gives each new employee an orientation covering the facility's policies, the program description, resident rights, emergency and fire procedures, abuse reporting, infection control and the employee's job duties, and records the orientation on a signed sign-in sheet.

The Administrator assigns the first 20 hours of direct care training before the employee works alone. These hours include 6 hours of dementia care and 4 hours on postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice.
Until the first 20 hours are complete and documented, the new employee works only under direct observation of a trained staff member and is not counted as sole staff on any shift.

The Administrator schedules the second 20 hours so they are completed within 4 weeks of hire. The second 20 hours include the remaining 6 hours of dementia training so that the person has 12 hours of dementia training in total.

Training is delivered by a qualified trainer. The Administrator records the trainer's name and qualifications, the date, the topic, the hours, and the employee's signature on a training record placed in the personnel file.

A staff member does not assist with resident medications until the hands-on portion of medication assistance training is complete. For a facility with 15 or fewer beds, the training is 10 hours (6 hours hands-on before assisting and 4 hours within 2 weeks of hire) plus an exam. For a facility with 16 or more beds, it is 24 hours (16 hours hands-on before assisting and 8 hours within 4 weeks) plus an exam.
The Administrator confirms the staff member passed the medication assistance exam and files the certificate. Staff who fail the exam do not assist with medications until they pass.
Each staff member who assists with medications completes 8 hours of medication assistance training every year, and the Administrator tracks the due date.
Each care staff member provides a first aid card or certificate from a qualified provider. The Administrator arranges first aid training if the person lacks it and tracks the expiration date.
The Administrator tracks each direct care employee's annual 20 hours (including 8 hours on dementia) on a training matrix, reviews it monthly, and assigns missing hours before the anniversary date.
The Administrator holds a current administrator certificate (80-hour program with at least 60 hours live and the state exam within 60 days of completion). Verification is described in SB-02.
The Administrator completes 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia, and keeps the certificates. The Governing Body checks the CE status at least annually.
Annually, the Administrator reviews the in-service training plan (SB-04) and updates it for observed needs, incidents, and regulatory changes.
The Administrator reviews each staff member's performance at the end of orientation and annually, and documents the review in the personnel file.
If training is overdue, the Administrator removes the person from the affected duties until the training is done, documents the action, and reports compliance status to the Governing Body.

responsibilities.duty: Plans, delivers or arranges training, tracks hours, verifies documentation, and restricts duties when training is incomplete.

responsibilities.role: Direct care and medication assistance staff
responsibilities.duty: Attend training, pass exams, hold first aid cards, and perform only tasks for which they have been trained.
Funds training time, verifies the administrator's certification and CE, and reviews the training matrix.
Provide qualified instruction and sign records with their qualifications.

documentation: Orientation sign-in sheet and checklist
Training records with date, topic, hours, trainer qualifications and employee signature
Medication assistance training certificate and exam result
First aid card or certificate
Training matrix with due dates
Administrator certificate and CE certificates
Annual performance review

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All personnel, including the administrator, direct care staff, kitchen, housekeeping and maintenance staff, and volunteers who work in the facility
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease by confirming that each employee has been screened by a physician, including tuberculosis (TB) testing, and is protected from workplace exposure to bloodborne pathogens.
policies.policy: All personnel need a physician health screening, including a chest x-ray or an intradermal TB test, within 6 months before or 7 days after employment (22 CCR §87411(f)). [AGENCY NAME] records the screening on LIC 503 for staff. Exposure control follows the facility's written infection control plan (LIC 9282), which names an Infection Control Lead, and OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030 (22 CCR §87470). Results are kept in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: The health screening report completed by a physician for each staff member.
A skin test for tuberculosis infection, read by a qualified health professional.
Contact with blood or other potentially infectious material through broken skin, mucous membrane, needlestick or other means during work.
The person named in the infection control plan who is trained by a qualified professional and oversees infection control.

procedures: At the offer stage, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) gives each candidate LIC 503 and explains that the screening must be done within 6 months before or 7 days after the start date.
The candidate takes LIC 503 to a physician. The physician examines the candidate, documents the TB test or chest x-ray result, and signs the form.
The candidate returns the completed LIC 503 to the Administrator, who reviews it for physician signature, date, TB result and any restrictions.

If the screening has not been done before hire, the Administrator confirms an appointment and tracks the 7-day deadline from the first day of work. The Administrator does not allow the employee to continue working after day 7 without a completed screening.

If a TB result is positive or a chest x-ray is abnormal, the Administrator does not allow the person to work in direct contact with residents until a physician documents in writing that the person is not contagious. The Administrator keeps the physician's statement in the file.
The Administrator files LIC 503 and supporting results in the personnel file and records the screening date on the personnel record.
The Administrator arranges any follow-up screening that Title 22, the physician, or the local health department requires and tracks the due dates.

Employees tell the Administrator promptly if they have symptoms of TB or another communicable disease (for example, a persistent cough, fever or night sweats), and the Administrator refers them to a physician and removes them from work until cleared.

The facility follows its infection control plan (LIC 9282) for staff illness, hand hygiene and use of personal protective equipment. The Infection Control Lead trains staff at hire and on an ongoing basis.

For any employee who may be exposed to blood or body fluids, the Administrator offers hepatitis B vaccination at no cost within 10 working days of assignment under 29 CFR 1910.1030, or documents the employee's written declination.
The facility provides personal protective equipment, sharps containers and cleaning supplies at no cost to staff, and trains staff on their use at hire and annually.

After any exposure incident, the employee stops the task, washes the area, and reports immediately to the Administrator. The Administrator arranges a confidential medical evaluation and follow-up, and documents the event.
The Administrator keeps exposure-related medical information separate and confidential, and releases it only as law allows.
The Infection Control Lead and Administrator review the plan annually, after any outbreak declaration, and when the licensing agency asks, and update employee health practices as needed.
During annual file audits, the Administrator confirms that every active employee has a completed LIC 503 and corrects any gap immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Collects and reviews health screening reports, tracks deadlines, restricts work when required, and arranges exposure follow-up.
Trains staff on exposure control and maintains the infection control plan.
Complete screening on time, report symptoms and exposures, and use protective equipment.
Completes and signs LIC 503 and documents TB screening results.

documentation: LIC 503 health screening report
TB test or chest x-ray result and any physician clearance statement
Hepatitis B vaccination record or declination
Exposure incident report and follow-up record
Infection control plan (LIC 9282) and training records
Annual personnel file audit

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator and all employees; personnel files kept by the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and confidential personnel file for each employee, available to the licensing agency, showing that every person is qualified, cleared, screened and trained.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a personnel file for each employee as required by Title 22. Each file contains the personnel record (LIC 501), the criminal record statement (LIC 508), proof of criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer, the health screening report with TB results (LIC 503), a first aid card, training documentation and sign-in sheets, and the job description and supervision lines (22 CCR §87411; LIC 281, Sections A and B, items B4 and B5). Training documentation, including trainer qualifications, is stored in the personnel record. Personnel files are kept in a locked location at the facility and are made available to the licensing agency on request. The facility keeps job descriptions and personnel policies on file.

definitions.definition: The form that records the employee's identifying information, position, dates of employment and qualifications.
The set of records kept on each employee, described in this policy.
The documented reporting structure showing who supervises each position.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) opens a personnel file for each new hire before the first shift and prepares a file checklist listing every required document.
The employee completes LIC 501 and the Administrator checks it for accuracy and completeness, including position, hire date and qualifications.
The Administrator files LIC 508 and the proof of clearance, exemption or transfer, and notes the date on the checklist (see ST-02).
The Administrator files the completed LIC 503 with TB result and any physician clearance (see ST-04).
The Administrator files a copy of the first aid card or certificate and notes the expiration date.
The Administrator files the signed job description and the supervision chart, so that each employee has a written statement of duties and who supervises them (see SB-03).
After each training, the Administrator files the training record: date, topic, hours, trainer's name and qualifications, and the employee's signature, along with the class sign-in sheet (see ST-03).
The Administrator files medication assistance training certificates and exam results for each employee who assists with medications.
The Administrator files performance reviews, disciplinary notices, and the employee's signed acknowledgment of personnel policies.

The Administrator keeps all personnel files in a locked cabinet or secure electronic system, limits access to the Administrator and designated staff, and does not release information except as law permits or the employee authorizes.
The Administrator reviews every personnel file at least once each quarter against the checklist and records missing or expiring items, due dates and corrective actions.

The Administrator keeps files for former employees in a secure location for the period required by Title 22 and other applicable law. Before destroying any file the Administrator confirms the required retention period with the licensing agency or legal counsel and documents the decision.
The Administrator makes personnel files available to the licensing agency during inspections or on request, and records who reviewed them and when.
The Administrator updates the personnel file within 5 working days of any change, such as a new certification, name change or position change.
The Governing Body reviews a summary of personnel file compliance at least annually.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers, contractors and students at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set clear standards for how staff treat residents and handle resident property, so that residents' personal rights are protected and abuse, exploitation and boundary violations are prevented and reported.
policies.policy: Staff protect each resident's dignity and keep residents free from punishment, humiliation, intimidation and abuse, and they use each resident's preferred name and pronouns (22 CCR §87468.1). Staff do not discriminate against any resident on the basis of actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status in admission, room or restroom assignment, association or any other matter. Staff do not handle resident cash and do not accept gifts from residents or families except under the resident funds policy (RR-04) and the safeguards in 22 CCR §87217. Staff are mandated reporters under W&I Code §15630 and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately. Violations lead to discipline up to and including termination.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates appropriate staff behavior from personal, financial or other relationships that could harm or exploit a resident.
A care custodian or facility staff member who must report known or suspected elder or dependent adult abuse.
The name and pronouns a resident asks staff to use, which may differ from legal records.
Taking or using a resident's money, property or services improperly.

procedures: During orientation, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) reviews this policy and the resident personal rights with each employee. The employee signs an acknowledgment that is placed in the personnel file.
Staff address residents by their preferred names and pronouns, and the preference is recorded in the resident's needs and services plan and shared with all staff.
Staff treat residents with courtesy, knock before entering rooms, protect privacy during personal care, and give residents choices in daily routines.

Staff never use punishment, threats, ridicule, name-calling, shouting, withholding of food, care or visitors, or any other humiliating or intimidating behavior. Staff who are frustrated ask another staff member to step in and then tell the Administrator.

Staff do not treat any resident differently because of sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status, and do not disclose these facts without the resident's consent, except as the law requires.

Staff do not borrow money, accept loans, or take gifts of cash or valuable items from residents or families. Staff report any offer of a gift to the Administrator, who decides whether it may be declined or accepted under the resident funds policy and documents the decision.

Staff do not hold, manage, spend or keep resident cash. Any resident cash held by the facility is handled only by the Administrator or a designated person under the written safeguards, with receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as residents' money, as described in RR-04.
Staff do not use resident property, vehicles, phones or accounts for personal use, and do not sell items to or buy items from residents.
Staff do not enter into romantic or sexual relationships with residents, do not make sexual remarks, and do not post images or information about residents on social media or personal devices.

Staff do not accept appointments as a resident's agent, trustee, executor or beneficiary, and do not witness financial or legal documents for residents, without prior written approval of the Administrator and the Governing Body.

If a staff member suspects or sees abuse, neglect or exploitation of a resident, the staff member immediately protects the resident and makes the report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then submits the written report (SOC 341) within the statutory time, as set out in SP-01 and W&I Code §15630. The staff member also informs the Administrator, but the Administrator's approval is not required to report.
The facility does not retaliate against any staff member who reports in good faith. Anyone who discourages, delays or interferes with a report is subject to discipline.

The Administrator investigates every boundary or conduct complaint promptly, removes the employee from contact with the resident if safety is a concern, documents the findings, and reports to the licensing agency and other agencies as required (see SP-02 and REC-02).

Discipline for violations may include coaching, written warning, suspension or termination, depending on the severity. Abuse, theft and exploitation lead to immediate removal from duty and may result in referral to law enforcement and licensing boards.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually with all staff and records attendance in the training log.

responsibilities.duty: Trains staff, enforces the policy, investigates complaints, imposes discipline and makes required reports.
Treat residents with dignity, keep boundaries, avoid handling resident cash, and report suspected abuse.
Supports enforcement and reviews serious conduct cases.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy
