policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: Administrator, staff who create or use resident records, and the person responsible for medical and administrative records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate, secure and accessible record for each resident and a current register of residents, and retains and destroys records in line with Title 22 and other applicable law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a record for each resident and a register of residents as Title 22 requires. The resident record contains the admission agreement, the pre-admission appraisal, the medical assessment, the needs and services plan, any advance directive, and the inventory of the resident's personal property. The admission agreement is signed and dated within 7 days of admission and the resident receives a copy immediately (22 CCR §87507). The pre-admission appraisal and consent are completed before admission (22 CCR §87457). Medication records are kept at least 1 year and medication destruction records at least 3 years (22 CCR §87465). Dementia advertisements are kept for 3 years. The facility does not apply a general retention period to resident records until the Administrator has confirmed the period required by Title 22 and written it into the retention schedule. If HIPAA applies to the facility, it follows the administrative requirements of 45 CFR 164.530.

definitions.definition: The file for each resident, containing admission, assessment, care planning, medical, medication and property documents.
A current list of residents with identifying information and admission and departure dates, kept as Title 22 requires.
The written list of record types, how long each is kept, and how it is destroyed.
Any advertisement or marketing material that describes the facility's dementia or memory care services.

procedures: At the time of pre-admission contact, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) opens a record for the prospective resident and files the pre-admission appraisal, the evaluation of functional, mental and social needs, the consent, and the written suitability determination (see AD-01).
The Administrator ensures that the physician's medical assessment is obtained before or at admission and filed in the record.

The Administrator ensures that the admission agreement is signed and dated within 7 days of admission, gives the resident or representative a copy immediately, and files the signed original in the record (see RR-03).
When the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability, the Administrator files the LIC 9158 with the record.
The Administrator files the needs and services plan, each reassessment and each plan update with the date and the signatures of the resident or representative (see AD-02).

The Administrator files any advance directive, resuscitation request or other medical orders the resident provides, and notes their location on the face sheet so staff can find them in an emergency (see RR-05).
At admission, staff and the resident or representative prepare an inventory of the resident's personal property. Both sign it, and staff update it when items are added or removed (see RR-04).
The Administrator maintains the register of residents and updates it on the day of each admission, transfer, discharge or death.

Staff record medication assistance, PRN medications, and refusals in the medication record. The Administrator keeps these records at least 1 year and keeps medication destruction records, signed by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, at least 3 years (see HS-01).
The Administrator keeps copies of each dementia advertisement, including the date and place it was used, for 3 years.

The Administrator reviews the Title 22 record-keeping and retention requirements (22 CCR §87506 and the related register provisions), writes the retention schedule, and has it approved by the Governing Body. Until that schedule is approved, no resident record is destroyed.

Resident records are kept in a locked location or secure electronic system at the facility, accessible only to authorized staff, and available to the licensing agency, the resident, and the resident's representative as law allows (see RR-06).

If the facility is a HIPAA covered entity, the Administrator designates a privacy official, trains staff, maintains privacy policies and complaint and sanction procedures, and documents compliance under 45 CFR 164.530.

When a resident leaves, the Administrator completes the record, files the discharge notice and any transfer documents, returns the resident's property with a signed receipt, and moves the record to closed storage.

Closed records are retained under the approved retention schedule and are then destroyed by shredding or secure deletion. The Administrator records the destruction date and method. No record is destroyed if it is part of an investigation, complaint or legal action.
The Administrator audits a sample of open and closed resident records every quarter for completeness and signatures, and records findings and corrections.

responsibilities.duty: Opens, maintains, secures, audits and retains resident records and the register, and approves any destruction.
Document care, medication assistance and changes accurately and promptly, and protect confidentiality.
Approves the retention schedule and reviews audit results.
Oversees HIPAA administrative requirements.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) locations in California; the Administrator, designated Reporting Officer, all direct care staff, and the governing body or corporate officers
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every report, notice, fee payment and certification renewal required by California law to the CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, the local health officer, the local fire authority, law enforcement, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and the person responsible for the resident. Each must be made accurately, on time, and be documented.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will make all reports and notices required by Title 22 and the Health and Safety Code on time. The reporting timeframes are set by 22 CCR §87211 (C7) and the abuse reporting law, W&I Code §15630 (C25). The Administrator is responsible for reporting. If the Administrator is absent, the designated Reporting Officer or the staff member in charge acts under this policy. No staff member may delay or hold back a required report to wait for an investigation, to avoid embarrassment, or because a family member asks. Reports are factual and complete. Staff who suspect abuse are mandated reporters and must report personally; telling a supervisor does not meet that duty. The agency will also pay license fees on time (HSC §1569.185, C28) and keep the Administrator's certification current (HSC §1569.616, C21). Under this policy:

(1) Within 7 days, a written report goes to the licensing agency and to the person responsible for the resident after any death, any serious injury as determined by a physician, any use of an automated external defibrillator (AED), or any incident that threatens the welfare, safety or health of a resident (including an unexplained absence or psychological abuse).
(2) Within 24 hours, a report by phone or fax goes to the licensing agency and the local health officer for any outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe or major accident.
(3) Fires and explosions are reported immediately to the local fire authority and to the licensing agency no later than the next working day.
(4) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult is reported to the local ombudsman, the licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if there is serious bodily injury, and within 24 hours in all other cases. A written SOC 341 follows.
(5) Written notice goes to the licensing agency within 2 business days of any foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice, and applicants are informed before they sign.
(6) The licensing agency is notified within 30 days of a new administrator and within 15 working days of a change of chief corporate officer.
(7) The annual license fee is paid on each license anniversary, and a $25 capacity change fee is paid when capacity changes.
(8) The Administrator's certificate is renewed every 2 years with 40 hours of continuing education.

definitions.definition: The California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Community Care Licensing Division, Adult and Senior Care Program (ASCP), through the regional office that serves the facility. Statewide ASCP business line: (916) 657-2592. Regional office: [PHONE].
The resident's authorized representative, conservator, agent under a power of attorney, or family member or other person identified in the admission agreement and resident record as the contact.
The staff member designated in writing by the Administrator to make reports under this policy when the Administrator is unavailable. Name: [REPORTING OFFICER NAME].

An injury that a physician determines to be serious. If a physician has not yet assessed the resident, the facility treats the injury as reportable when there is any doubt, and files the 7-day report.
For abuse reports, an injury that triggers the 2-hour reporting deadline. When staff are unsure whether an injury is serious, they report within 2 hours.
The written report form for suspected abuse of an elder or dependent adult, sent after the telephone report.
The county or city public health officer who receives reports of outbreaks and poisonings. Contact: [PHONE].

procedures: Immediate safety first: Any staff member who discovers a death, injury, fire, poisoning, suspected abuse or other emergency first protects the resident, calls 911 if needed, and notifies the Administrator or person in charge right away. Reporting duties begin when the event is discovered, not when the review is finished.

Report-clock log: The Administrator or person in charge records the date and time the event was discovered on the Reporting Timeline Log and works from that time to calculate each deadline in this policy.

Sort the event by type: The Administrator or Reporting Officer uses the Reporting Matrix (kept in the front of the Reporting Binder) to decide which of the following apply: (a) death, serious injury, AED use or threatening incident; (b) outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe or major accident; (c) fire or explosion; (d) suspected abuse; (e) financial, administrator or corporate officer notice. One event may trigger several reports.

Deaths, serious injuries, AED use and threatening incidents (7 days): Within 7 days of the event, the Administrator completes the written incident report, sends it to the licensing agency and to the person responsible for the resident, and keeps a dated copy. Staff do not wait the full 7 days if the facts are known sooner. Unexplained absences and suspected psychological abuse are included. Details are completed under SP-02.

Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents (24 hours): Within 24 hours of discovery, the Administrator reports by phone or fax to the licensing agency and to the local health officer. The Administrator records the name of the person spoken to, the date and time, and the information given, and follows up with a written report. Infection outbreaks are managed under SP-07.

Fires and explosions: Staff call 911 and evacuate under SP-06. The Administrator notifies the local fire authority immediately (if not already responding) and notifies the licensing agency no later than the next working day. The notice is documented with date, time and the person contacted.

Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult, 2-hour reports: If the suspected abuse involves serious bodily injury, the staff member who knows of or suspects it reports by phone to the local ombudsman, the licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours. The Long-Term Care Ombudsman CRISISline is 1-800-231-4024; local ombudsman: [PHONE]; local law enforcement: [PHONE].

Suspected physical abuse, 24-hour reports: If there is no serious bodily injury, the same three agencies are reported to within 24 hours. Staff do not wait for proof. Reasonable suspicion is enough. Staff are mandated reporters and make the report personally; telling the Administrator does not replace it.

Written abuse report: After the phone report, the reporting staff member completes the SOC 341 within the time required by law and sends it to the required agencies. The Administrator checks that it was sent and files a copy in the incident file, not in the personnel record of the accused. Prevention and investigation are covered under SP-01.

No retaliation and no screening: The Administrator may not screen, delay, edit or discourage a staff member's abuse report and may not retaliate against any person who reports. Any such attempt is reported to the governing body and may be grounds for discipline.

Financial notices (2 business days): Within 2 business days of receiving a foreclosure notice, unlawful detainer notice, bankruptcy filing, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice, the Administrator or the owner sends written notice to the licensing agency. The Administrator also tells the governing body the same day. The facility must pay a civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000, if it fails to give required notice.

Notice to applicants: Before an applicant or the person responsible for the applicant signs an admission agreement, the Administrator tells them in writing about any financial notice covered in step 11 that is outstanding, as required by 22 CCR §87211. This is coordinated with RR-03.

New administrator (30 days): When a new administrator is hired or appointed, the governing body or outgoing Administrator sends written notice to the licensing agency within 30 days. The notice includes the new administrator's name and a copy of the current administrator certificate (see SB-02).

Change of chief corporate officer (15 working days): When the chief corporate officer changes, the governing body notifies the licensing agency in writing within 15 working days, and any related updates to legal entity records are filed (see SB-01 and GOV-02).

Annual license fee: Before each license anniversary, the Administrator pays the annual fee: $495.60 for facilities licensed for 4 to 6 beds or $742.80 for facilities licensed for 7 to 15 beds. A 50% late fee applies to late payment. The Administrator sets a calendar reminder 60 days before the anniversary and records the payment date, amount and check or confirmation number.

Capacity change fee: Before the facility increases or decreases licensed capacity, the Administrator submits the request to the licensing agency and pays the $25 capacity change fee. Residents are not admitted above the capacity shown on the current license.

Administrator certificate renewal: The Administrator tracks the certificate expiration date and completes 40 hours of approved continuing education, including 8 hours on dementia, every 2 years, then submits the renewal and the fee (currently $140 per state guidance) to the Administrator Certification Bureau, phone 916-653-9300, before expiration. Initial certification requires the 80-hour program (at least 60 hours live) and the state exam within 60 days (HSC §1569.616).

Quarterly review: Each quarter the Administrator reviews the Reporting Timeline Log against incident reports, resident records, the fee and certificate calendar and corporate records to find any missed or late report. Any gap is corrected immediately, reported to the governing body, and handled through GOV-03.

Retention: Copies of every report, notice, fax confirmation, phone log entry and proof of payment are retained in the Reporting Binder and, where they relate to a specific resident, in the resident's record (see REC-01), for the period required by that policy.

responsibilities.duty: Makes or oversees every report and notice in this policy; maintains the Reporting Timeline Log, Reporting Matrix and Reporting Binder; pays license and capacity fees; renews the administrator certificate; reviews timeliness each quarter.
Acts for the Administrator when the Administrator is unavailable; notes discovery times; makes time-critical phone reports (24-hour, 2-hour, fire).

responsibilities.duty: Helps identify reportable conditions, such as serious injuries, outbreaks and poisonings, and supports the incident review. This role does not replace the Administrator's reporting duty.

documentation: Reporting Timeline Log showing the discovery date and time of each event, the report type, the deadline, the date and time reported, who reported, and the agency and person contacted

required_items.text: LIC 200 - Application for a Community Care Facility or Residential Care Facility for the Elderly License. Form filled out completely; all applicants sign, including each general partner; original signatures only (no photocopied signatures); signatures match the applicant's name unless the applicant is a corporation or LLC; if a corporation applies, the Board resolution authorizing the signers must be submitted with the form.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A1 p.3

required_items.text: LIC 215 - Applicant Information. One form completed by each applicant; original signatures; reference statements must be current and should not be from relatives.

LIC 308 - Designation of Facility (Administrative) Responsibility. At least one individual must be designated to act in the licensee's absence; a licensee cannot designate himself or herself; a corporation or LLC must submit a resolution authorizing the delegation; original signatures.

LIC 309 - Administrative Organization. Not required of individual applicants; required if the applicant is a corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC; information must match the LIC 200; terms of office should match articles/bylaws.
LIC 400 - Affidavit Regarding Client Cash Resources. Form completed with the appropriate box checked; make sure a bond is obtained if needed; original signatures.

LIC 402 - Surety Bond. Must use the LIC 402 language; State of California identified as beneficiary; effective and expiration dates; original seals and signatures; bond amount must match the amount on the LIC 400.

LIC 401 - Monthly Operating Statement. Number of clients corresponds to requested capacity; other facility income clear and documented; operating costs indicated and reasonable (salaries at least minimum wage); approximately 25 percent of salaries added for fringe benefits (or explain why not); rent matches lease/rental/mortgage payment; separate LIC 401 for each other licensed facility; indicate estimated or actual; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 401a - Supplemental Financial Information. Part I (other income and expenses, excluding facility income) completed by individual applicants and each general partner; Part II completed by all applicants; preparer name and original signature.

LIC 403 - Balance Sheet. Complete the LIC 403a first; reflect assets and liabilities of all owner activities; figures must be 'realistic'; life insurance at cash/surrender value; real estate shown per applicant type; on-site furnishings and equipment at market value; only cash and cash equivalents count toward the three-month start-up funds; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 403a - Balance Sheet Supplemental Schedule. Detailed balance sheet completed before the LIC 403; cash in the bank verified with the LIC 404; liabilities verified by credit report; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 404 - Financial Information Release and Verification. Used to verify approximately three months of operating funds; a verifiable line of credit is acceptable if readily accessible; start-up funds should not be consumed on renovation or repair; the financial institution must send the verification directly to the licensing agency (the licensee cannot hand-carry it); one form or set per bank; all persons on an account sign; accounts in the applicant's name; original signatures.

LIC 500 - Personnel Report. Show all planned employee positions, with days and hours of duty (reviewed for required staff coverage for all hours of operation); list the Director/Administrator and any staff already hired; list unhired positions as 'to be hired' by position title; reverse side signed if there are fingerprint-exempt personnel; separate LIC 500 for each other licensed facility; original signatures.

LIC 501 - Personnel Record. Only for those who do not complete an LIC 215; submitted with the application only for directors/administrators who are not licensees; other staff forms are kept on file at the facility.

LIC 503 - Health Screening Report - Facility Personnel. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator; for RCFE applicants the screening must be less than six months old at the time of application; must be signed and dated by a qualified medical professional (no photocopied signatures); TB test portion completed including result, or separate test verification attached.
LIC 508 - Criminal Record Statement. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator.

required_items.text: LIC 610D (RCFE only: LIC 610E) - Emergency Disaster Plan. The plan must show two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate the number of residents; if the applicant does not currently occupy the property, use of the relocation site requires authorization from the agency or person in possession, verified in writing.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A14 p.9

required_items.text: LIC 999 - Facility Sketch. Dimensions and use of all rooms; door and window exits shown, with exit routes indicated by number as on the LIC 610 Emergency Disaster Plan; rooms for non-ambulatory residents and staff identified; sketch of all indoor and outdoor space (driveways, fences, storage, gardens, recreation areas); separate sketches per building plus one overall sketch for multi-building sites; outdoor sketch shows dimensions, location of major equipment and swimming pools, and utility shut-off locations.
LIC 9054 - Fire Inspection. Listed as 'Required' for RCFE in the Section A table; no further instruction text appears for A16 in LIC 281.
Partnership Agreement / Articles of Incorporation / Articles of Organization. Required for RCFE; it tells the licensing agency who is ultimately responsible for which functions in the facility.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B1 p.11

required_items.text: Partnership: a written agreement is not necessary when partners are husband and wife; two individuals not related by marriage must provide a partnership agreement.

Partnership: determine whether it is a general or limited partnership; for a limited partnership only the general partner(s) are on the license, but names and addresses of limited partners are also needed.
Partnership: all general partners need to be on the license and sign the application; name and business address of each general partner is needed.
Partnership: a description of the obligations and duties of each general partner and whether or not each can act on behalf of the others.

Articles of Incorporation: establish the applicant is a valid corporation qualified to do business in California; a seal from the state of incorporation should be attached; foreign (out-of-state) corporations must also provide a Certificate of Qualification from the California Secretary of State.
Corporation: constitution and by-laws (day-to-day operation).
Corporation: Board Resolution identifying the agents acting for the corporation, including authorization to apply for a license and the person authorized to sign and act on its behalf.
Corporation: directors' and officers' names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers; name and address of 10 percent shareholders.
Articles of Organization (LLC): stamped by the Secretary of State; a foreign LLC must also submit Secretary of State Form LLC-5 stamped by the California Secretary of State.

LLC: operating agreement; names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers of all managing members, managers, and non-managing members holding a 10 percent or more interest. If the signer is not identified in the operating agreement as having authority, a written delegation of authority consistent with the operating agreement is necessary.

Verification of Administrator Qualifications - For RCFE only: proof of registration in a 40-hour certification program submitted with the application; a Department-issued certificate verifying completion of the 40-hour RCFE certification program by an approved vendor is required prior to licensure.
Education: transcripts from an accredited school, when required; for out-of-country schools, class descriptions or college catalog, or certification of class equivalency from a local college.

Experience: written references obtained by the applicant/licensee and submitted (showing the person worked there, in what capacity, specific duties, and for what period); if references cannot be obtained, a declaration signed by the Administrator stating why and the same details.
Verification of experience for an applicant applying for a one to six bed ARF or RCFE is not necessary.

Job Descriptions - a job description for each staff classification; there must be a job description for each classification listed on the LIC 500, and staff positions must correspond to those listed on all personnel reports.
Each job description must address: duties and responsibilities.
Each job description must address: minimum qualifications that correspond to licensing requirements, including any special licenses, certificates or special skills needed for the job.
Each job description must address: lines of supervision (supervision given and to whom, and supervision received and from whom).
Personnel Policies - work hours/shifts documenting positions that provide coverage with competent staff, corresponding with the positions, work days and hours on all personnel reports.

Personnel Policies - abuse reporting procedures; documentation must indicate employees will be informed of their responsibilities to report to the licensing agency as well as to the police and child/adult protective agency.

Personnel Policies - hiring practices, including screening for necessary education and experience, and informing employees that conditions of employment include fingerprint clearance, statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, physical examination/health questionnaire, and child abuse index check.

In-Service Training for Staff - a plan for in-service training submitted at the time of application, as part of the plan of operation. New employee training: a description of the training and who will conduct it.

Ongoing training: topics to be covered (the list should include administrator continuing education units); how often the training will be given; how the training will be documented; must include topics specified in the regulation sections listed (for RCFE: 87565 Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly Regulations; 80065 General Regulations also listed).
Program Description (CCF/RCFE) - brief statement of the purpose, goals and program methods (program philosophy). A pamphlet or brochure is acceptable if all of the elements B7.1-B7.11 are included.
Days and hours of operation.
Daily schedule of activities provided by the facility, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
A one month schedule of planned social, educational and recreational activities, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
Description of the basic services provided by the facility (see Admission Guideline LIC 604 or 604A for a list of basic services).
Description of the optional services provided in the facility as listed in the admission agreement.
Description of how the facility will handle medical emergencies if a client becomes ill or injured.
Procedure for handling and assisting clients/residents with self-administered medications.
Transportation arrangements.
Description of community resources and consultants to be used by the facility.
A procedure (approved by the licensing agency) for immediate response to incidents and complaints.

Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights (titled 'Discipline Policies' in the text) - personal rights applies to all facility categories. The detailed discipline-policy content in the document is for group homes and foster family agencies only.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B8 p.17

required_items.text: The Department evaluates the discipline policies to ensure they do not violate personal rights and that there is a clear statement that no corporal or unusual punishment will be used; further information may be requested if the statements are unclear.

Admission Policies - persons accepted for care, including age range and compatibility determination process, when necessary. Overall, the policies must provide ages of clients, rates and refund policies, acceptance and retention limitations, pre-admission appraisals, needs and services plans, medical assessments, and an admission agreement.
Intake procedures for placement in group homes (listed in the document's B9 list; it names group homes only).
Criteria for assessing appropriateness of placement given an individual client's needs (interviews, procedures for obtaining and developing the necessary paperwork, etc.).
Needs and services plan.
Client's Rights/Personal Rights (at a minimum a statement that residents will be informed of their rights and that their rights will not be violated).
Medical assessment.
Pre-admission appraisal plan.
Emergency information.
Sign-in and sign-out procedures.
Immunization requirements.
Physical examination requirements (including TB testing).
Sample Menu - planned meals and snacks for one week, with foods from the four basic food groups.
Sample Menu - portion sizes.
Sample Menu - times meals served.
Control of Property - name and address of the owner of the property.

Control of Property - a copy of the lease or rental agreement (no requirement on length). If the agreement precludes use as a facility or operation is contrary to its terms, the license must be denied/withdrawn.
Control of Property - proof of ownership if the applicant owns the property (property tax bill, deed or other document containing the facility street address).

Bacterial Analysis of Water - only if the facility gets water from a well or other private source (required at initial licensure regardless of number of clients): evidence of on-site inspection of the source and a bacteriological analysis by a local or state health department or other qualified laboratory establishing the water is safe; analysis signed by a qualified agency representative.

Insurance Information (RCFE only) - a statement on whether there will be insurance covering the facility operation; if so, the type of coverage and with whom; if none, a statement of such is sufficient.

Theft and Loss Policy (RCFE only) - must include provisions for inventory of personal property at admission, modification of the inventory, practices to safeguard personal property upon the death of the resident, documentation and reporting of loss of personal property, method of marking personal property, and method for providing a secure area for safekeeping of resident personal property.

Neighborhood Complaint Policy - procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints, including a time when the owner, licensee or designee will be available to meet with neighborhood residents. The text says it is applicable to non-resident owner community care facilities providing care for six or fewer persons only; the Section B table marks it 'Required' in the RCFE column.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B15 p.20

required_items.text: First Aid Card - staff providing direct care and supervision must receive first aid training from qualified persons (e.g., American Red Cross); copies of first aid cards for applicant/administrators must be submitted and will be verified.
Orientation Certificate - proof of attendance must be submitted with the application.
Final checklist: Have you attended an orientation for your facility type and submitted a copy of your orientation certificate(s)?
Final checklist: Is your application (LIC 200) signed and dated by all applicants?
Final checklist: Do you have an Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610)?
Final checklist: Do you have a Facility Sketch (LIC 999) showing indoor/outdoor space as well as all exits?
Final checklist: Have you completed all Financial Information to operate your facility?
Final checklist: Have you enclosed your application fee?
Final checklist: Be sure all necessary information is completed, properly signed (original signature) and dated.

official.notes: LIC 281 has no single 'plan of operation' form. The application fee plus Section A and Section B documents go to the licensing agency as one packet. Per LIC 281, submit them in the same sequence as the booklet. An incomplete packet is returned in full. All forms need original signatures and dates, and the applicant should keep a photocopy. The reviewer compares documents against each other: job descriptions (B4) must match the LIC 500; work hours in the personnel policies (B5) must match the personnel reports; and the exit routes on the LIC 999 must match the LIC 610 plan. Organize the manual by B-number in this order: B1, B2, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 (only if the water supply is private), B13, B14, B15, B16, B17. B15 (neighborhood complaint policy) is marked 'Required' for RCFE in the table, but the B15 text limits it to non-resident-owner facilities of six or fewer. B9 includes a group-home intake bullet, and B8's discipline detail is for group homes and FFAs only. B7 says its '**' items may also appear in 'Section B10 - Admission Policies'; the document most likely means B9. Newer program-specific plan-of-operation content, such as the infection control plan and the dementia and hospice waivers listed in your regulations, is not in LIC 281. Use the Title 22 sections you listed (87208 plan of operation and others) as supplements. The CDSS forms page lists the current edition as LIC 281 (11/25), which I could not retrieve, so confirm the numbering against it before filing.
